title: The scientists behind the data: investing in Europe’s data stewardship workforce
content:
EMBL brings together international partners to professionalise research data management across domains and sectors

By Isabela Paredes Cisneros and Lisa Vollmar 

Research data is only as valuable as the expertise and culture that support it. Yet across Europe, the professionals most responsible for enabling high-quality, reusable research data – data stewards – often work without standardised career paths, consistent training, or formal recognition. A new Horizon Europe project is designed to change that.

STARDAST – STewardship And Recognition for DAta Science Talent – is a four-year, €8 million Coordination and Support Action coordinated by the European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL) and set to begin in September 2026. 

Bringing together 19 partner institutions across nine countries, including research infrastructures, universities, and companies, STARDAST combines expertise from life sciences, particle physics, linguistics, translational medicine, biodiversity, digital humanities, and industry R&D within a single, coordinated framework.

title: Why Reading Egyptian Hieroglyphics Is Easier Than You Think
content:
We’ve featured Egyptologist Ilona Regulski here on Open Culture a few times before. Once, she explained how to read ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs; another time, she told us what the Rosetta Stone actually says. It was, perhaps, inevitable that she would cross paths with Rob Watts, creator of the YouTube channel RobWords, whose videos we often post. When he made the journey to Berlin’s Neues Museum, and specifically to its Egyptian Museum, Regulski was the expert he sought out to tell him — and us — all about how hieroglyphs, literally “sacred carvings,” actually make words.

Faced with a stone chiseled full of hieroglyphs, where do we start? Ancient Egyptian texts are all read from top to bottom, but some go left to right, and others right to left. To know which way, Regulski says, we must first look for symbols with a clear front and back, such as those in human or animal shapes.

title: An (Extremely) Fond Farewell to Dolly Parton, Library Friend and Children’s Literacy Champion
content:
Dolly Parton, the beloved country music legend and pop culture icon who died Tuesday, was also a tireless advocate for children’s literacy whose Imagination Library was given one of Library’s highest honors, part of her long association with the national library.

In the 2021 Library of Congress Literacy Awards, the Imagination Library, an initiative of Parton’s Dollywood Foundation, was awarded the David M. Rubenstein Prize of $150,000 for the program’s phenomenal national and international success.

“Dolly Parton’s work was precisely what we envisioned this prize rewarding,” Rubenstein said. “A well-run, highly dedicated literacy program that operated both with passion and a clear sense of mission. It was a privilege to know her and her work.”

The program started in Parton’s home county in rural east Tennessee in 1995 with 1,760 children under age 5 enrolled. Each child received one free book mailed to their home monthly for up to 60 months; therefore each child would have their own library when they started first grade.

title: Ukrainians Embrace God but Shun Moscow Orthodoxy
content:
Polling suggests the war has made Ukrainians more religious. But a closer look at more than two decades of data suggests a more complex picture.

While 12 years of Russian aggression have strengthened religious commitment among a significant minority of Ukrainians, the relationship between religious faith, church affiliation, and national identity has changed dramatically.

The share of Ukrainians describing themselves as believers increased to 71% in 2010, from 58% in 2000, according to Razumkov Centre research. Between 2010 and 2020, the share remained around 70%, though it rose during periods of crisis, to 76% in 2014, for example, following Russia’s occupation of Crimea and the beginning of the war in Donbas. 

After Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022, the share rose again to 74%, before falling to 70.5% in 2023 and 68% in 2024.

This pattern suggests war and acute social stress temporarily increased the number of people who identified as religious, but the increases did not necessarily become permanent. It has not been a straightforward wartime religious revival.
snippet: Polling suggests the war has made Ukrainians more religious. But a closer look at more than two decades of data suggests a more complex picture.

title: Ajankohtainen kybersääntely finanssialalla 8.9.2026
content:
Dittmar & Indreniuksen ja Helsinki Fintech Farmin tapahtumasarja saa jatkoa. Syksyn ensimmäisessä aamiaistilaisuudessa pureudumme ajankohtaisiin aiheisiin finanssialan kyberturvallisuudesta. title: Apple threat notifications and spyware: what everyone should know
content:
Since 2001, Apple has been warning its users when they may have been targeted by spyware, using email, iMessage, and banners in their accounts. But in September of this year, the company began to place these threat notifications directly in users’ device Lock Screen and Settings — making them harder to miss. Here’s what you need to know about Apple threat notifications and spyware attacks in general, and what they mean for your digital security.

Put simply, that Apple detected activity in your device signalling that you have been targeted  with so-called mercenary spyware, that is, the sophisticated commercial surveillance technology that is sold by companies like NSO Group, Paragon, or Cytrox, often exclusively to government clients.

This alert does not tell you whether or not the spyware attack succeeded, nor does it provide information about who might be behind the attack or what their motives may be. Further analysis is required for you to see a clearer picture.

title: A List of ICE Subpoenas to Tech Companies
content:
Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has conducted unlawful investigations into dozens of individuals who have documented ICE activities in their communities, social media users who criticized the government, and international students who attended a protest.

A favored tool in these speech chilling investigations are administrative subpoenas sent to technology companies, requesting basic subscriber data about their users. For example, from 2018 to 2020, ICE sent nearly 500 administrative subpoenas to Meta, Google, and Twitter (now X), according to documents obtained by Just Futures Law. In just the second half of 2025, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) sent 21 administrative subpoenas to Reddit, according to its Transparency Report.

While some subpoenas are routine, ICE has been forced to withdraw others after users challenged them in court or companies pushed back. These challenged subpoenas exceeded the agency's statutory authority and violated users' First Amendment rights.

title: Meta’s mega-deal could change the game for social media
content:
Meta’s multibillion-dollar court settlements with U.S. states Wednesday set the stage for groundbreaking changes to protections for children across social media — a realm where Congress has tried and failed to regulate.

The total dollar amount — $18 billion, including $17 billion from a sprawling case based in California, plus a separate agreement with Texas — would make it one of the largest consumer protection settlements in U.S. history.

But its real power would come from the age limits and other safety guardrails that Meta would impose on its Instagram and Facebook platforms, terms that could someday extend to companies such as Google, TikTok and Snap.

Indeed, Meta immediately issued a public plea for TikTok and Google-owned YouTube to “join us and state attorneys general in adopting this new standard, to ensure teens use social media in a healthy and responsible way.” Meta is launching a campaign to “shame” other companies into signing on to the provisions, according to a person with knowledge of the plan who was granted anonymity to disclose private conversations.

title: Haiti: Justice and protection urgently needed following deadly armed gang attack in Kenscoff
content:
Amnesty International condemns the massacre that took place during the night of 23–24 August in Kenscoff, near Port-au-Prince. At least 47 people were killed and 22 injured, according to the United Nations, while dozens of people were reportedly abducted. Those attacked reportedly included people displaced by violence who had sought refuge in a church.

“Sadly, we are once again witnessing another massacre in Haiti. This is a reminder of the devastating human cost of the absence of effective policies to protect the population. We urge the Haitian authorities and the international community to redouble their efforts to protect people from the escalating violence by armed gangs. Anyone suspected of criminal responsibility for these killings, abductions and other serious human rights abuses must be identified and brought to justice in fair trials,” said Astrid Valencia, Deputy Regional Director for Research for the Americas at Amnesty International.

title: Thousands of little penguins will be vaccinated against bird flu down under
content:
H5N1 virus spreading quickly in Australia with coastal birds and other wildlife threatened

Originally published on Global Voices

Screenshot – ABC NEWS video: Thousands of little penguins on Phillip Island to be vaccinated for bird flu.

The arrival of H5N1 bird flu in Australia presents serious challenges, especially for wildlife. While bird flu has been plaguing the rest of the world for years, Australia had been free of the virus until a case was identified on June 20.

News that numerous wild birds had died from the virus prompted authorities to launch a vaccination campaign, with Victoria’s little penguin colonies at St Kilda and Phillip Island top of the list.

Julie Old, Associate Professor in Biology, Zoology and Animal Science, Western Sydney University, explained the vaccination process in an article with The Conversation:

Capturing wildlife to vaccinate them is difficult, particularly because the bird flu vaccination requires they be caught twice, for two doses. However, little penguins are flightless, live in colonies and return at night to the same burrow, making them easier to capture and vaccinate.

title: Not Even Risk of Torture Deters Trump Administration Deportations
content:
A US federal judge ordered the US government on August 21 to take back a Mexican man the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) had deported to Mexico based on a diplomatic assurance from the Mexican government that he wouldn’t be harmed. An immigration judge had previously found the man to have a significant chance of being tortured if returned to Mexico and thus granted him “deferral of removal.”

According to a New York Times report, the man had helped US law enforcement authorities by testifying against Mexican cartels, testimony that would put his life in danger if returned. Given the brutal power of the cartels, the Mexican government’s assurances in this case are downright phantasmic.

In fact, diplomatic assurances regarding torture are not worth the paper they’re printed on. These are formal promises by one government to another about how well they will treat a person being deported or extradited. Torture is a serious crime, often taking place in dark corners: police station basements, prison holding cells, or remote border checkpoints. Nearly all countries – 176 in total – have signed the Convention against Torture and no government admits to torturing or condoning torture.

title: Substitute Sounds for Noise
content:
By Jonathan Power

LUND, Sweden | 26 August 2026 (IDN) –Everyone has their favourite sounds- a ball on a cricket bat on a summer’s afternoon, birds singing, waves breaking on the beach, the coffee pot perking on the stove, children playing Scooby-Doo. Mine are the quiet sounds of the English Lake District- William Wordsworth’s:

“A flock of sheep that leisurely
pass by one after one;
the sound of rain and bees
murmuring; the fall of rivers,
wind and lakes, smooth fields;
white sheets of water, and pure sky.”

Noise is less and less sweet sounds. It is cars and trucks, aeroplanes and builders, canned music in cafes, a symphony playing an atonal concerto. Some pop music makes so much noise that pure sounds no longer exist. Noise is the excreta of technological civilisation. One study predicts that exposure to loud music will cause 50 million Americans to suffer heavy hearing loss by 2050. Ex-President Bill Clinton has long worn a hearing aid because, in his youth, he enjoyed loud music.

content:

title: How Romanians Get Their News: Facebook Leads, TV Wins on Trust
content:
A new analysis by the think tank Expert Forum (EFOR), based on a survey conducted by the Political Rating Agency, paints a more nuanced picture of how Romanians consume information and how social media interacts with traditional news media.

The main finding is that while digital platforms have fundamentally changed how news reaches audiences, they have not replaced traditional sources of information.

Survey data show that television remains the news source Romanians trust the most. Radio and online news outlets also enjoy levels of credibility comparable to – or even higher than – social media platforms.

At the same time, Facebook, TikTok, and YouTube have become key gateways through which people discover news. The gap between where people first encounter information and the sources they actually trust reflects one of the defining shifts in today’s media landscape.

title: A Student Said He Was a Hobby Plane Spotter. He Was Allegedly Taking Photos for the Chinese Government
content:

The Chinese official repeatedly told the student to destroy the SIM cards they used to communicate and stick to a Huawei phone.

The records provide insight into how Chinese state actors continue to use students to essentially crowd source imagery of sensitive U.S. locations or military aircraft, and how those students are told to remain undetected.

Seamus Hughes of Court Watch first identified and posted the records on Wednesday. 

Weiheng Zeng is an undergraduate student at the University of Waterloo, Ontario, Canada and has crossed into the U.S. around two dozen times since 2022, according to an affidavit from an FBI Special Agent.

title: ‘I Had No Involvement. Zero.’: Accused Mastermind Denies Killing Maltese Journalist
content:
The Maltese businessman accused of commissioning the 2017 car-bomb assassination of investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia took the stand to adamantly deny ordering her death, even as he admitted to delivering tens of thousands of euros to the plot's middleman and passing along leaked police intelligence.

"I never ordered the murder of Daphne Caruana Galizia," the defendant, Yorgen Fenech, told jurors during four days of testimony. "I had no involvement. Zero."

Fenech, 44, former chief executive of the Tumas Group and a major shareholder in a state power consortium, unexpectedly waived his right to remain silent to deliver his first public account of the crime since his 2019 arrest. He claimed Keith Schembri, the influential former chief of staff to former Prime Minister Joseph Muscat, framed him.

Schembri, who testified earlier in the trial, has denied any involvement, and police told jurors he was never considered a suspect.

title: The Costly Blunders in the Army’s $533 Million Fiasco
content:
The U.S. Army paid General Dynamics $533 million for an artillery factory that failed to produce a single usable shell.

Instead of efficient, state-of-the-art production lines, half a billion dollars in taxpayer funding paid for machines that kept failing in bizarre ways, former workers told ProPublica’s Jesse Coburn. Giant robot arms would catch fire. The Texas factory’s signature device often cracked the steel meant for the shells. And workers regularly had to take a sledgehammer to certain machines to try to make them function properly. But the machines still botched nearly every shell.

The boondoggle, which included a real-life dumpster fire, was described as an “absolute disaster,” by one former official who worked in an Army office overseeing the project. The official, like others interviewed for the story, spoke on the condition of anonymity.

In a detailed statement, the Army told ProPublica it exercises “rigorous oversight” and that, “where vendors fail to meet contract specifications” — as at the General Dynamics artillery factory — ”we are evaluating contract performance, seeking recoupment of funds, and pivoting resources.”

title: What has the return-to-office movement taught us? People, not technology help companies get ahead
content:
We like to believe that whatever ails a company can be fixed by digitising it. And technology is easy to swap. Rip out the old system, bolt in the new one, declare yourself modern. But a company is not its buildings, its machines, or its software. It is the people in it. Organizations do not change. People change or they quietly refuse to, and no amount of technology overrides that.

I learned this the hard way, leading corporate restructuring as a CFO and a CEO. You can redraw an org chart over lunch. Getting the human beings inside it to actually move forward is the real job, and there is no tool that will do it for you. The recent return-to-office wave is showing this right now, at enormous scale.

Through 2025 and into 2026, the big employers ordered everyone back. Amazon, around 350,000 people, full-time. JPMorgan Chase, remote work gone. Dell, hybrid scrapped. Mass change programs, imposed from the top, and look what they produced. Corporate guidance firm Gartner found nearly three quarters of HR leaders reporting internal tension.

title: Sissi Mattos aloittaa Maailman Kuvalehden pyöräilevänä kirjeenvaihtajana – Nelihenkinen perhe matkustaa maata pitkin kohti Keski-Aasiaa
content:
Sissi Mattos vastaa puhelimeen Italiasta, Cervignano del Friulin kunnasta läheltä Slovenian rajaa. Perhe on pysähtynyt pyörämatkallaan leikkipuistoon tauolle ja suojaan helteeltä. 

Mattosin nelihenkinen perhe on lähtenyt liikkeelle tandempyörillään kesäkuun lopussa Ranskasta, polkenut sieltä Sveitsin halki Italiaan ja aikoo sen jälkeen suunnata Slovenian kautta Balkanille, sieltä Keski-Aasiaan ja mahdollisesti Kiinaan asti.  

Jossakin vaiheessa he palaavat ehkä takaisin Eurooppaan ja matkustavat laivalla Mattosin miehen kotimaahan Brasiliaan. Matkaan on varattu vuosi – tai enemmän. Se selviää myöhemmin. 

Samalla Mattos kirjoittaa Maailman Kuvalehdelle juttusarjaa ihmisistä, joihin hän matkallaan törmää, sekä heille tärkeistä esineistä. 

Haastatteluhetkellä, elokuun puolivälissä, Mattosien päiväohjelma on jo rutinoitunut. 

Yöt vietetään pääosin teltassa. Aamulla Mattos ja hänen miehensä Rodrigo purkavat perheen teltan ja pakkaavat kaikki tavarat kahden tandempyörän selkään. 

”Siinä menee yllättävän kauan, helposti pari tuntia, kun lapset leikkivät samalla.”

title: Is the Trump Treasury panicking over the level of US debt?
content:
With the federal deficit near 6% of GDP and the national debt over $40tn, America’s fiscal position looks increasingly precarious

  • Bessent ‘will lose’ battle with bond markets, ex-mentor warns

    • Bessent ‘will lose’ battle with bond markets, ex-mentor warns

    Are we seeing the first signs of panic in Donald Trump’s Treasury? The US is by far the world’s biggest debtor, and the steady rise in global long-term interest rates – which I have long argued was inevitable – is starting to cause real pain.

    Until now, the Treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, has dismissed concerns about US debt, which recently surpassed $40tn, as a big nothingburger. Growth, in his telling, will be so spectacular the US will easily be able to meet its interest obligations without any significant tax rises or spending cuts, while the rest of the world will happily keep feeding it money. But if Bessent really believes that, why is he trying to strong-arm the bond market by fiddling with the maturity structure of government debt?

title: Nepal-Tibet floods: when disaster strikes before communities recover from previous climate extremes, crisis escalates
content:
Major flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border have destroyed homes, roads, bridges and local hydropower projects. The flooding of the Bhote Koshi river is affecting 50,000 residents. More than 100 people are dead, with hundreds more, including international tourists, missing.

This region of the Himalayas had not yet recovered from the Bhote Koshi flooding in 2025 that killed nine people as it washed away a “friendship bridge” linking Nepal and China, disrupting trade and transport for months.

In Sri Lanka, recent floods and landslides struck affected communities that were still recovering from Cyclone Ditwah, which had caused widespread damage only nine months earlier. With little time to recover from the cyclone, communities had no protection from further flooding. More than 15,000 people have been directly affected and 6,800 people were displaced this August.

Disaster risk usually considers how severe the next flood, wildfire, cyclone or drought will be. But the Nepal and Sri Lanka examples show another dimension that is often overlooked: how quickly can a community recover and will it do so before the next disaster arrives?

Tiede etsii totuutta, mutta kaikki kysymykset eivät ehkä ole tieteellisesti ratkaistavissa. Ratkaisemattomuus voi tarkoittaa joko sitä, ettei kysymykseen ole oikeaa vastausta, tai sitä, ettei mitään vastausta voida perustella riittävällä todistusaineistolla.

title: Climate change exposes 580 million children to 20 extra ‘heat-stress days’ every year
content:
More than 40% of children under the age of 10 globally are already experiencing at least 20 additional “heat-stress days” due to climate change.

This is according to a new attribution study, published in Science Advances, which combines climate models with demographic data to assess the age groups and regions that are exposed to the most hot, humid days.

The study finds that children up to the age of nine already face more additional heat-stress days globally as a result of climate change than any other age group. 

It adds that south Asia, southeast Asia and west Africa are recording the greatest childhood exposure to dangerous levels of humid heat – largely because these regions have a rapidly growing population with the highest proportion of young children.

As the climate warms, children will continue to be more exposed to heat stress than any other age group, the paper warns.

The lead author of the study tells Carbon Brief that the findings should inform discussions about climate justice, noting that children in developing countries “have contributed the least to historical greenhouse gas emissions”.

title: Meta’s settlement will compel others to bend the knee and set up teen guardrails
content:
Instagram and Facebook’s parent company agreed to sweeping alterations and a payment of up to $18bn to settle a landmark trial

Meta’s agreement to change how teenagers use its social networks marks a major turning point for the US tech giant, setting a precedent that could significantly reshape how other social media operates in the coming years.

Meta agreed to substantial alterations to Instagram and Facebook on Wednesday as part of a settlement to end a landmark lawsuit. Dozens of US states had accused it of addicting and harming children with dangerous products. The company also agreed to pay up to a combined $18bn over a decade to several US states and territories involved in the suit.

title: Food system resilience: Why Agricultural Production Diversity matters for our food supply
content:
APD can be thought of as an agricultural equivalent of biodiversity. Rather than measuring the diversity of species within an ecosystem, APD measures the diversity of agricultural production. There are several ways to calculate APD, but in our study we used a methodology borrowed from ecology, the Shannon Diversity Index.

The Shannon Diversity Index is a mathematical measure that captures both the quantity and relative abundance of different species, or in our case, different agricultural products. It considers not only how many types of produce are grown, but also how evenly production is distributed among them. The result is a single value that can be compared across regions and over time to assess changes in production diversity.

APD has proven to be an important indicator of food system resilience. A diverse agricultural sector is generally better able to withstand external shocks such as droughts, pests, diseases, or market disruptions. Simply put, diversity increases the likelihood that some forms of food production will continue even when others are affected by a crisis.

title: Konstnären Nastja Säde Rönkkö inleder tvåårigt performanceverk i Astra / Taiteilija Nastja Säde Rönkkö aloittaa kaksivuotisen performanssiteoksen Astrassa
content:
Den 2 september inleds konstnären Nastja Säde Rönkkös performanceverk here with you i Astra i Åbo. Under de kommande två åren kommer verket att utvecklas genom möten mellan konstnären och människor som vistas i byggnaden.

here with you är ett deltagarbaserat konstverk där besökarna bjuds in att påverka innehållet. Den första onsdagen varje månad mellan klockan 8 och 18 finns Rönkkö på plats i Astra. Vem som helst kan be henne utföra en handling, ett uppdrag eller en gest som känns meningsfull i stunden, något som sedan blir en del av det växande konstverket.

– Jag är intresserad av vad som uppstår mellan människor när vi stannar upp och ger tid åt varandra. Konstupplevelsen behöver inte alltid handla om att betrakta ett fysiskt objekt. Den kan också uppstå i ett möte, säger Nastja Säde Rönkkö.

Rönkkö är en internationellt verksam konstnär som arbetar med performance, video, text och installationer. Hennes verk har visats på bland annat Sydney Opera House, Royal Academy of Arts i London och Kiasma i Helsingfors. I sitt konstnärskap utforskar hon frågor om närvaro, gemenskap, teknologi och vad det innebär att vara människa i vår tid.

title: Dolly Parton’s “Jolene” Slowed Down to 33 RPM Sounds Great and Takes on New, Unexpected Meanings (RIP)
content:
Note: We were sad to see the news that Dolly Parton passed away. Today we are bringing back one of our favorite Dolly Parton posts. She will be missed.

The Walrus is… Dolly Parton?

Not every record yields gold when played backwards or spun more slowly than recommended, but a 45 of Parton’s 1973 hit “Jolene” played at 33 RPM not only sounds wonderful, it also manages to reframe the narrative.

As Andrea DenHoed notes in The New Yorker, “Slow Ass Jolene,” above, transforms Parton’s “baby-high soprano” into something deep, soulful and seemingly, male.

In its original version, the much-covered “Jolene” is a straight up woman-to-woman chest-baring. Our narrator knows her man is obsessed with the sexy, auburn-haired Jolene, to the point where he talks about her in his sleep.

Apparently she also knows better than to raise the subject with him. Instead, she appeals to Jolene’s sense of mercy:

You could have your choice of men

But I could never love again

He’s the only one for me, Jolene

title: What Counts as Safe AI?
content:
AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic, and IBM now boast an addition to their AI safety and security credentials: ISO/IEC 42001 certifications.

The certificate confirms that the companies have established a process to identify and manage AI risks. Although it does not guarantee that OpenAI’s ChatGPT will always produce accurate answers, that Anthropic’s Claude cannot be misused, or that Alphabet’s Gemini is free from bias, it gives nervous corporate customers something valuable: evidence that an outside auditor has examined a company’s AI management and meets the standard.

That’s enough to turn ISO 42001 into AI’s first global trust mark.

title: EFF's Policy Position on ALPR Surveillance: Eliminate It and Reduce Its Harms
content:
Automated license plate readers (ALPRs) build a searchable map of everywhere a driver goes, fed into databases that police, ICE, and private vendors can query after the fact. Networked across a city, ALPRs are purpose-built to track everyone regardless of suspicion. ALPRs are not a surveillance tool that can be made safe with the right policy or feature update—they are irredeemably harmful.

EFF's position is that ALPR mass surveillance—the indiscriminate, continuous collection and retention of location data on every driver, regardless of suspicion—should not exist. Because it nonetheless does, EFF also urges courts and state legislatures to impose strict, enforceable restrictions, such as warrant requirements and deletion deadlines.

title: Meta agrees to pay $17B, adopt kids’ safety features to resolve US lawsuits
content:
SACRAMENTO, California — Meta has reached a tentative $17 billion settlement with nearly all U.S. states that would also see the social media giant make sweeping changes to dramatically restrict minors’ access to Instagram and Facebook, the California Department of Justice announced Wednesday.

The pending agreement is a monumental concession without precedent by one of the world’s wealthiest and most powerful tech companies. It would end a pivotal trial over claims brought by California and more than two dozen other states that Meta intentionally hooked kids on its platforms, while misleading users about their potential harms. The deal would also resolve claims brought by other states and some U.S. territories in different proceedings.

“We have secured a settlement with Meta that will make social media less dangerous for our kids and make a world of difference for children and their families,” California Attorney General Rob Bonta said in a statement. He said the terms of the deal call for “massive transformations that will reduce the risk of harm.”

title: In Cameroon, before the scroll, there was the dance floor
content:
In Cameroon, ‘bals dansants’ are annual community dance gatherings organized during the holidays

Originally published on Global Voices

From children to elders, bals dansants bring generations together through music and dance. Photo by Julienne Honba. Used with permission

By Julienne Honba

Every holiday season, young people from Ebolowa in southern Cameroon and surrounding villages gather for community dance nights that combine entertainment, socializing, and economic activity.

In Ebolowa, Cameroon, it’s already late when the music finally gets loud — loud enough to draw people toward the dance floor. The village of Olem, in the Mvila Department, in the South region of Cameroon, is usually quiet at this hour. But on July 26, the night of their annual dance gathering, the atmosphere is different. Young people have traveled from nearby communities, some coming directly from Ebolowa, for a night that many have been looking forward to for months.

title: Bolivia’s NGO Registry Threatens Human Rights Work
content:
Bolivia’s government published two decrees in early August that threaten the right to freedom of association and the work of human rights defenders. 

One decree states that non-governmental organizations must register with the Vice-Ministry of Public Investment and External Financing before carrying out any project that involves “technical or financial cooperation,” regardless of the source of funding. Organizations must renew their certification every three years and complete an annual update.

The same Vice-Ministry will be charged with evaluating whether the organization’s objectives align with the “country’s development plans.” If it deems them unaligned, the Vice-Ministry can order unspecified “corrective measures”.  

Bolivian officials have framed the new registry as part of a broader modernization effort and have cited the Financial Action Task Force’s (GAFI) anti-money laundering standards as justification. However, the decree goes much further than reasonable measures to ensure transparency and prevent money laundering.

title: Around the world, people are rejecting divisive and dangerous politics. We can – and must – build on that | Gordon Brown
content:
The vast majority of the global public wants international cooperation on human rights, climate and AI. Like-minded countries must stand together to deliver

Britain’s new prime minister, Andy Burnham, is already having to make one of his gravest decisions. He has to issue the instructions that he alone gives to the military, setting out the UK response in a doomsday scenario of a nuclear weapons attack on us. He will, as I did two decades ago, sign a piece of paper telling commanders whether or not to retaliate and, if so, whether through targeting civilian conurbations or military sites. These instructions are written down in the aptly named “letter of last resort”.

Now, more than at any time since the 1960s Cuban missile crisis, the European public fears a third world war. With the nuclear Doomsday Clock developed by atomic scientists moving ever closer to midnight, and Japan, South Korea, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Egypt, Poland and Germany contemplating either acquiring nuclear weapons or siting them on their soil, our world is descending from a rules-based order to a power-based one, where might is deemed right and brute force dominates.

title: Civil Defence in Poland: What to Do When Sirens Sound and Drones Are in the Air
content:
The war in Ukraine has made questions that seemed purely theoretical just a few years ago much more real. Repeated incidents involving missiles and drones near or inside Polish airspace show why it is worth knowing what to do when a threat appears over your home.

So what should you do when the sirens suddenly go off? Head to the basement? Get in your car and leave? Wait for an RCB Alert? What if the message never arrives? And who is actually responsible for warning and protecting you?

The answers lie in two rather bureaucratic terms: population protection and civil defence.

Put simply, it is a system designed to make sure that people are not left on their own when a crisis hits.

And it is not just about shelters. Civil defence also means detecting threats, warning the public, organising evacuations and rescue operations, securing water and food supplies, keeping communications running, and making sure emergency services and public authorities are prepared.

There is an important distinction here. As Poland’s government security guide explains, in peacetime Poland operates a population protection system. If martial law is declared or war breaks out, this system becomes civil defence.

title: Scientists Discover Vast Underground 'Anomaly' on Mars
content:
Scientists have discovered a thermal “anomaly” deep underground on Mars that could help explain the red planet’s divided geography and shed light on whether it once hosted alien life, according to a study published Wednesday in Nature.

Using a novel approach involving three Martian orbiters, the team peered into the interior of the planet and detected that its mantle—the layer between its crust and the core—is 400 to 750°F hotter in the southern hemisphere compared with its northern half.

The temperature anomaly could help explain the longstanding mystery of the so-called “Martian dichotomy,” the term for the bizarre difference between the Martian north and south hemispheres. Whereas Mars’ northern half is dominated by lowlands that may have once hosted a giant ocean, the southern half is covered in highlands that are miles higher in average elevation.

title: Armenian Court Orders Son of Ex-President Held in Sweeping Graft Probe
content:
A court in Yerevan ordered the eldest son of former Armenian President Robert Kocharyan held in pretrial detention on Wednesday, expanding a sweeping corruption investigation that has ensnared the former leader and several high-ranking ex-officials.

The decision to hold Sedrak Kocharyan for two months followed his detention on Tuesday alongside his father. Investigators carried out coordinated raids on family-linked real estate and commercial holdings, escalating a long-running political battle between Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan and the country's former ruling elite.

Lawyers for the younger Kocharyan said they would appeal the ruling, with defense attorney Alexander Kochubayev describing the case as an "extralegal prosecution" driven by political motives.

Armenia’s Anti-Corruption Committee stated that the elder Kocharyan, who served as president from 1998 to 2008, used his office to acquire state property at artificially low prices and accept substantial bribes. Officials said several prime parcels of land were improperly funneled to the family and later developed into commercial ventures.

title: Idaho Law Protects Faith Healers. It Wasn’t Always That Way.
content:
In Idaho, parents who say their faith prohibits lifesaving medical care for their children can’t be charged with child neglect or manslaughter. Supporters of this protection over the years have included lawmakers who voiced support for “traditional” Idaho values.

But from at least the 1880s through the early 1970s, it was illegal for parents in Idaho to choose prayer over medical care when a child’s life was at stake, newspaper archives and historical documents show.

“Every parent of any child who willfully omits, without lawful excuse, to furnish necessary food, clothing, shelter, or medical attendance for such child, is guilty of a misdemeanor,” reads the 1887 edition of Idaho territory statutes, published before statehood.

The statutes included no mention of spiritual belief as a “lawful excuse.” Three years later, the state constitution explicitly put limits on Idaho’s freedom of religion. It would not excuse “acts of licentiousness,” polygamy or other practices “inconsistent with morality or the peace or safety of the state.”

title:
Europe recycles just 12% of the materials it
uses. Here’s how training can accelerate the transition to a circular economy
content:
Since January 2024, ten organisations in four European countries have been working on the following question: If Europe is serious about circular economy, who is actually going to teach people how to run one? Become, short for Boosting Circular Economy Expertise through learning communities, is a project that was designed to do just this. Co-funded by Erasmus+, it runs until mid-2027, bringing together four universities, two vocational colleges and four employers from across Finland, the Netherlands, Slovenia and Bulgaria.

The consortium first mapped existing and missing circular skills in its four regions. The gap analysis that was carried out was then backed up by the development of modular training materials and a training week in Bled (Slovenia) in May 2025 for around thirty educators, followed by a second week for twenty company practitioners in March 2026. Circular hubs and local learning communities are also operating in all four countries.

title: Sunscreen for lakes and dams: could a thin floating layer of nanomaterial shield water from evaporation?
content:
Water stored in dams and reservoirs for humans to use often evaporates, especially in hot regions like southern Africa. Rising temperatures speed evaporation up, leaving less water for people, farming and industry. Daniel Kwasi Kpeglo has just completed a PhD in physics. He explains his laboratory research into a new design – a thin nanomaterial floating cover that could be placed over lakes and dams like a blanket, reducing evaporation by limiting the amount of infrared heat from the sun that reaches the water. He also outlines what hurdles need to be cleared for the design to be tested in the real world.

Reducing evaporation simply means wasting less of the water we already have. The idea behind my research was quite simple: if we can keep more of the water that we have already stored, we reduce the pressure to find new sources of water.

This is especially relevant for Africa, where water stored in dams and lakes can make an important contribution to water security, food production and resilience to drought.

Kela ajautui johtajuuskriisiin syksyllä 2025. Laitoksen tuolloinen uusi pääjohtaja Lasse Lehtonen oli kiristänyt etätyösääntöjä ja kommentoinut Kelan työtapoja tavalla, jonka henkilöstö koki epäluottamuslauseena osaamistaan ja työkulttuuria kohtaan.

title: Vihreät: lapsiperheköyhyydestä eroon vuoteen 2035 mennessä
content:
Vihreät vaatii sitoutumista lapsiperheköyhyyden poistamiseen vuoteen 2035 mennessä.

Vihreän eduskuntaryhmän varapuheenjohtajat Saara Hyrkkö ja Inka Hopsu peräänkuuluttivat eduskuntaryhmän kesäkokouksessa, että Suomi sitoutuu poistamaan lapsiperheköyhyyden vuoteen 2035 mennessä. Kansanedustajat kritisoivat hallituksen politiikkaa, jonka seurauksena yli 26 000 lasta on työnnetty köyhyyteen, ja esittävät keinopaketin, jolla suunta voidaan kääntää.

Suomessa elää noin 137 000 lasta pienituloisissa perheissä. Tavoitteen toteuttaminen edellyttäisi uskottavaa suunnitelmaa, jonka ensiaskeleet tulee ottaa jo tulevassa budjettiriihessä.

"Suomesta on tullut lasten luokkayhteiskunta. Lasten eriarvoistuminen alkaa jo kohdussa ja jatkuu läpi elämän. Jo lähes joka seitsemäs lapsi asuu köyhässä perheessä, ja valitettavasti erityisesti lapsena koetulla köyhyydellä voi olla pitkä varjo. Suomi on näille lapsille velkaa paremman huomisen – ja se velka on huomattavasti valtionvelkaa vakavampi asia", Hyrkkö painottaa.

Hyrkön mukaan lapsiperheköyhyyttä ja köyhyyden periytymistä on torjuttava toimeentuloon, koulutukseen, harrastuksiin ja perheiden palveluihin liittyvillä keinoilla.

title: Wikimedia at Summer Institutes in Computational Social Science 2026 Uyo, Nigeria
content:
Twenty researchers, educators, health professionals, students, and practitioners gathered in Uyo with different research interests but a shared task: to learn how computational methods could help them investigate social problems more carefully.

For fourteen days, the Summer Institute in Computational Social Science Nigeria 2026 brought participants together under the theme “Tech for Open Minds.” The programme combined discussions on misinformation, gender bias, public health, education, digital inclusion, and knowledge inequality with practical training in data collection and analysis.

For many participants, it was also an opportunity to discover Wikimedia beyond reading Wikipedia articles.

The Summer Institute in Computational Social Science was founded by Professors Christopher Bail and Matthew Salganik, the SICSS Nigeria 2026 – Uyo experience was sponsored by the Templeton World Charity Foundation and Wiki In Africa. Hosted by Dr Rhoda Asuquo, with Dr Juliet Inyang and Yohanna Joseph Waliya as co-hosts. A handpicked group of exceptional facilitators facilitated each session, all experts in their respective fields.

title: OpenAI staff observed warning signs before AI agent hacking crusade caused global alarm
content:
Firm says ‘early signals … could have triggered an earlier response’ as it releases report into Hugging Face hack

OpenAI staff observed signs of rogue behaviour among its leading-edge AI agents weeks before they escaped their training environment to launch an unprecedented hacking crusade that spread global alarm.

The San Francisco AI company conceded on Wednesday that “early signals … could have triggered an earlier response”, as it released a report into the days-long July hack of a major software repository, Hugging Face, considered the first autonomous agent cyber-attack.

title: Lämmöllä-lehden päätoimittaja: Energiakriisi muutti suomalaisten suhdetta talotekniikkaan – nyt kiinnostavat kulutus, automaatio ja oman kodin energiaratkaisut
content:
Energiakriisi sai suomalaiset kiinnostumaan siitä, mitä omassa talossa tapahtuu

Degerlund nostaa pääkirjoituksessa yhdeksi merkittävimmistä muutoksista energiakriisin. Kun sähkön hinta oli suhteellisen edullinen ja vakaa, oman talon kulutusprofiili, lämpökäyrä tai sähkön tuntihinnat eivät kuuluneet kovinkaan monen pientaloasukkaan jokapäiväisiin puheenaiheisiin.

Tilanne muuttui nopeasti energian hinnan noustessa ja hintavaihtelujen kasvaessa. Samalla kiinnostus oman kodin energiankulutukseen, lämmitysjärjestelmän toimintaan ja energiatehokkuuteen kasvoi.

Nykyisin energian hintaan vaikuttavat muun muassa sää, energiantuotanto, siirtoyhteydet ja kansainväliset tapahtumat. Myös uusiutuvan sähköntuotannon lisääntyminen näkyy tavallisen kuluttajan arjessa esimerkiksi sähkön tuntihinnoissa.

– Suomalainen energia-arki on muuttunut vähän sellaiseksi, että aamulla katsotaan sääennusteen lisäksi sähkön hintaa – ja toisinaan molemmissa jännitetään aivan samaa asiaa: tuuleeko huomenna? Degerlund kirjoittaa.

Talotekniikan kehitys näkyy jo tavallisessa omakotitalossa

title: Panicked Putin Reaches for Nationalization Button
content:
Vladimir Putin has signed a decree allowing the state to seize refineries, telecom companies, and retail outlets if their owners fail to adequately protect against drone attacks. The threat of nationalization by a regime with a fondness for the Soviet era is generating fear among Russian businessmen and oligarchs.

According to the decree, almost every element of critical infrastructure, including private enterprises that are deemed crucial for the country’s security and the economy, can be “temporarily” taken into government ownership for an indefinite period.

Few doubt that the decision was a panicked response to recent Ukrainian drone attacks on oil facilities, which have caused a massive gasoline crisis, and on at least 21 warehouses belonging to Wildberries, a Russian version of Amazon, that have already killed at least 14 civilians and caused widespread fear.

title: Andy Burnham has to shape the UK’s social media ban. Australia and France could show him how.
content:
LONDON — As Britain’s children head back to school, its new prime minister needs to decide exactly how he wants to keep them off social media. 

Britain isn’t the only country crafting a social media ban for minors. Developments in Australia and France over the break should give Burnham’s ministers and officials plenty to think about. Australia’s ban is only having a limited effect on how much kids get on to social media, while France’s ban has hit a huge legal hurdle.

In June, then-Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced plans to ban social media for under-16s — only to resign a week later and leave his successor Andy Burnham with an in-tray of unanswered questions about a policy that upends the U.K.’s current online safety regime.  

MPs return to Parliament next week after the summer break, and Burnham’s government will need to decide how the ban — which is supposed to come into effect in spring — will work.  

Australia was the first country in the world to introduce a social media ban for kids in December last year. Last month, the Australian government published its first wave of findings on the experiences of more than 4,000 children and families since the ban took effect.

title: Cuba: More than 27,000 of solidarity letters reach Luis Manuel Otero Alcántara
content:
Following the symbolic delivery of more than 27,000 letters of solidarity to Cuban artist and activist Luis Manuel Otero Alcántara in private event at El Espacio 23 in Miami, Amnesty International said: 

“Today, thousands of messages of solidarity finally reached Luis Manuel Otero Alcántara in person. Each letter is a reminder that, even when the Cuban authorities tried to silence and isolate him behind prison walls, people around the world continued to stand with him demanding his freedom. 

Luis Manuel should never have spent a single day in prison for his art, his activism, or for peacefully expressing his views. His freedom today does not erase nearly five years of injustice, nor the fact that he was forced into exile. The Cuban authorities must release all those imprisoned solely for exercising their human rights and guarantee that Luis Manuel can return to Cuba, if he so chooses, without surveillance, threats or reprisals,” said Astrid Valencia, Deputy Director of Research for the Americas at Amnesty International.

title: 10 Prisoners Executed in Various Prisons
content:
According to HRANA, citing Iran Human Rights Organization, eight prisoners were executed in Borujerd Prison, Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad, Karaj Central Penitentiary, Semnan Central Prison, and Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan. Haalvsh also reported the executions of two additional prisoners in Isfahan Prison.

The prisoners have been identified as Sajjad Shirzadi, 34, married and from Kermanshah; Farshad Safari, approximately 40, married, father of one, and from Hashtgerd; Mahmoud Talebi, 44, from Torbat-e Heydarieh and father of one; Seyed Hossein Hesari, 35, from Mashhad; Lotfollah Ahmadvand, 38, from Aligudarz; Faramarz Baghbani, 46, father of two and from Borujerd; Hamed Emami, 39; and Mohammad Ali Kaffashi, 42.

According to the report, at dawn on Tuesday, August 25, Sajjad Shirzadi was executed at Karaj Central Penitentiary. He had been arrested approximately four years earlier on a murder charge and was subsequently sentenced to death by a judicial authority.

At dawn on Wednesday, August 19, Farshad Safari was also executed at Karaj Central Penitentiary. Safari had been arrested five years earlier on a murder charge and subsequently sentenced to death.

title: Zambia: Closing Courts Curbs Access to Justice
content:
(Johannesburg) – Zambian authorities suddenly closed and cordoned off the courts without credible explanation on August 24, 2026, effectively blocking the filing of any legal challenges to the results of the August 13 presidential election, Human Rights Watch said today. The authorities should immediately allow the courts to reopen.

Zambian police stated that the closures were an “intelligence-led and preventive measure,” without providing details. A notice from the chief administrator of the judiciary to court staff, seen by Human Rights Watch, said the court premises were closed “for security reasons.” The notice said guidance on opening the courts “will be issued in due course, once the situation is contained.” The courts’ closure coincided with the deadline to file any legal challenges to declaring the incumbent, President Hakainde Hichilema, the winner.

title: Flock’s CEO Is Lying to Cops About 404 Media's Reporting on Abortion Case
content:
In an August call with Ohio law enforcement and government officials, Flock’s CEO Garrett Langley repeatedly lied about his surveillance technology’s role in tracking a woman who had self-administered an abortion, the context around the tracking of the woman, and 404 Media’s coverage of that watershed incident. Langley claimed that the story is “entirely false,” despite court records, police reports, and 404 Media’s other reporting documenting the case in detail.

The candid comments were recorded by Signal Akron journalist Doug Brown, who sat in on the call with an Ohio lawmaker and then shared them with 404 Media. The recording shows how Langley speaks in private with government officials when the conversation is not intended to be broadcast, and comes amid a PR campaign to recast his embattled company. Recently Langley has gone on something of a media blitz, speaking to outlets like The New York Times and appearing on the tech-focused All-In Podcast. Those conversations were, obviously, meant to be consumed publicly. Behind the scenes, Langley speaks very differently.

title: Designed for Impact: The Next Evolution of OCCRP’s Website
content:
Welcome to the new OCCRP.org. Here’s what’s changed on our site — and how we hope it will better serve you. 

Following up on our previous website launch and brand refresh, we’re excited to share the next milestones: a new homepage, upgraded features, and a complete rebuild of the site’s underlying foundation — what we like to call the 'bones' of OCCRP.org. 

You will notice that the homepage is wider, the logo bolder, and that there’s generally more to see on the homepage. We want to make it easier to find what you’re looking for as well as be inspired by everything we have to offer.

We’ve rebuilt the site to be mobile-first, because that’s how most of you read our stories. Our editors can now embed source documents and interactive elements directly into articles, making our work more transparent. We’ve also updated our layouts to better showcase our storytelling in digital and audio formats. 

While the design changes are easy to see, even more has changed under the hood. This new infrastructure makes our site more nimble and ready for continuous updates down the road.

title: The ‘robot Olympics’ were spectacular – but will this technology end up helping humans?
content:
In the past few days your social media feeds may have been full of videos of humanoid robots sprinting, jumping and performing various incredible (and not so incredible) feats.

This is because the second World Humanoid Robot Games have just finished in Beijing.

It featured many incredible sights, but some of the more mundane events offered more insight into how this technology will eventually help humans.

Commonly referred to as the robot Olympics, this event started last year, when about 500 robots showed off their abilities in 25 events. This year’s version featured more than 2,000 robots competing in 50 events.

The robots that enter must be so-called humanoid robots: under the games’ rules they need a torso, two arms and two legs, an onboard power source and no trailing cables.

Half of the events are direct copies of the human Olympics and Paralympics: track and field, weightlifting, soccer and boxing.

Just like in the human Olympics, the crowd-pleaser was the 100 metre sprint. This year, two robots beat Usain Bolt’s world record of 9.58 seconds, with the fastest clocking 9.39 seconds.

title: Tätä ei olisi odottanut: puolustukseen esitetty lisäraha pillastutti kokoomuksen
content:
Keskustelu Suomen asevoimien rahoitustarpeen kattamisen keinoista näyttää hämmästyttävän vaikealta. Tai sitten päähallituspuolue on painanut viestinnässään paniikkinappulaa muista syistä kuin demarien esittämän puolustusveron takia.

Demarien ahneudella ei ole rajaa, päivitteli kokoomus viralliselta Instagram-tililtään, kun tietoja veroesityksestä alkoi maanantaina tulla.

Puolueen kansanedustajat ovat julkaisseet nyt sarjatulella saman kaavan mukaan monistettuja tiedotteita, joissa paheksutaan miten puolustushankintoihin korvamerkitty veropaketti tappaisi Suomen talouskasvun, karkottaisi pääomat ja veisi yrittämishalut.

Harva olisi uskonut, että ehdotus asevoimien tarvitseman rahoituksen varmistamisesta aiheuttaa maanpuolustusimagoaan korostavassa puolueessa näin ison paniikin.

Liioittelutarpeen taustalla voi olla puolueen hätä laskevista kannatusluvuista. Verotus on perinteisesti ollut kokoomuksen oikeistosiiven mielestä varkautta, ja siitä huutamalla voidaan saada empivät liikkuvat äänestäjät kääntymään takaisin puolueen tukijoiksi.

title: OmaSavon sähköinen ajanvaraus avautuu 26.8.
content:
Uusi OmaSavon sähköinen ajanvaraus avautuu asiakkaiden käyttöön 26. elokuuta iltapäivällä. Aikoja voi varata 1.9. jälkeiselle ajalle.

Asiakas voi varata ajan terveyskeskukseen sairaanhoitajalle, äitiys-, lasten- ja seksuaaliterveysneuvolaan, koulu- ja opiskeluterveydenhuoltoon sekä lasten ja nuorten puheterapiaan.

Sähköisessä ajanvarauksessa ei voi varata aikoja lääkärille.

- Julkisessa terveydenhuollossa asiakas ei voi suoraan varata lääkäriaikaa verkosta, vaan ensin tehdään hoidon tarpeen arviointi. Jos asiakas ei löydä tarvitsemaansa aikaa OmaSavosta, hän voi varata ajan viestit-palvelun kautta, puhelimitse tai terveyskeskuksen sairaanhoitajan chatin kautta, kehittämisasiantuntija Maija Kaipiainen kertoo.

Vapaita aikoja on saatavilla OmaSavossa sekä vastaanotolle että videovastaanotolle. Lisäksi asiakas voi varata ammattilaiselle soittoajan.

Kun asiakas varaa ajan, hän saa vahvistusviestin sähköpostiinsa, jos hän on lisännyt sähköpostin omiin tietoihinsa OmaSavossa.

Lisäksi asiakas saa tekstiviestimuistutuksen kaksi vuorokautta ennen varattua vastaanottokäyntiä. Videovastaanotosta tai soittoajasta ei lähetetä tekstiviestiä.

title: Opening Access to Cultural Heritage through Digitalization and Wikimedia Commons
content:
In 2025, Wikimedia Indonesia, through the GLAM Indonesia Grant, supported several projects that bring together cultural preservation work with digital technology. This program is aimed at researchers, practitioners of art and culture, archivists, and communities working in the fields of galleries, libraries, archives, and museums. One of the program’s goals is to produce works that can be openly shared with the public through Wikimedia projects.

In its implementation, the two GLAM Indonesia 2025 Grant projects demonstrate different approaches to reopening access to cultural heritage. Illuminating Manuscript Ornament: From Royal Frames to Digital Commons processes the ornamental designs of Nusantara manuscripts into open digital visual assets. Meanwhile, the Digital Archiving for Banda Cultural Museum focuses on the documentation and digital archiving of a museum’s collection in Banda Neira.

title: With the end of physical media in sight, gamers have had enough
content:
An increasing tension between players and publishers about ownership of titles could lead to a divestment from the system the big companies are trying to enforce

At the time of press, there is a well-publicised protest taking place in the video games community. PlayStation 5 owners are being encouraged to log off from their consoles between 23 and 30 August – no playing games, no downloading new titles. The motivating factor is Sony’s decision to cease physical game disc production from January 2028. After that, games will only be released as digital products. In an act of poor timing or wilful defiance, Sony chose this week to send out a mass email reminding customers of their PS5 terms and conditions: “The software is licensed to you, not sold,” states the relevant clause. “You are granted a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, and personal license to play … ” It knows, of course, that most customers won’t open the email, let alone read it.

title: Tampereen Teatterissa tanssitaan vesisateessa
content:
Tampereen Teatterissa nähdään tänä syksynä viisi ensi-iltaa: 1920-luvun Hollywoodiin sijoittuva säihkyvä musikaali Laulavat sadepisarat, Alexandre Dumas´n klassikko Monte-Criston kreivi, Florian Zellerin komedia Täydellinen lauantai, Petri Kotwican psykologinen jännitysnäytelmä Musta jää ja Arttu Ratisen musiikki-ilta Ikuinen uni. Omien esitysten lisäksi ohjelmistossa nähdään lukuisia vierailuesityksiä.

"Tänä syksynä sade tulee kerrankin Tampereen Teatterissa näyttämöltä eikä katosta, ja remontin jälkeen sanon sen sekä helpottuneena että myös aivan kirjaimellisesti", teatterinjohtaja Mikko Kanninen kertoo.

"Kun katson nyt näitä viittä ensi-iltaamme rinnakkain, niissä toistuu tämä sama teema: Joku on juuri saanut suunnitelmansa valmiiksi, ja sitten maailma päättääkin toisin. Frenckelissä Täydellisen lauantain Markus haluaa vain kuunnella levynsä rauhassa, Laulavien sadepisaroiden Don Lockwoodin ura murenee äänielokuvan alle ja Monte-Criston kreivin Edmond Dantès astuu vankilaan keskellä menestystään täysin syyttömänä. Teatteri on niitä harvoja paikkoja, joissa romahdukset kannattaa katsoa aivan loppuun asti.

title: French Top Court Gets It Right, Strikes Down Social Media Ban For Youths
content:
Earlier this month, France’s top court struck down the country’s legislation that banned social media use for people under 15 years old, which had been scheduled to take effect in January 2027. This is a welcome win for free expression, as we face a wave of countries and U.S. states seeking to pass similar laws banning young people from social media. 

In particular, the Constitutional Council’s decision focused on two components:

The Council ruled that the legislation banning under-15s from social media infringed on freedom of expression and communication in a manner that is not appropriate, necessary, or proportionate, which is required by Article 34 of the French Constitution. In particular, it stressed that the ban did not distinguish between different types of online services, and ignored the circumstances of individual users, such as their exact age, level of maturity, and family situation.

The evidence is clear: these are reckless and harmful laws that negatively impact all people, not just those under 15. These measures chill all users’ exercise of the right to free speech and expression online by imposing obstacles on sites or by wrongfully blocking people’s access outright.

title: How Osman Kavala’s treatment became emblematic of the dire human rights situation in Türkiye
content:
This week the Grand Chamber of the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) delivered a landmark judgment in the case of prominent Turkish human rights defender, Osman Kavala. 

It denounced the bad faith of Türkiye’s authorities, and ruled that Kavala has been unlawfully imprisoned for almost nine years based on a politically motivated trial. Consequently, the court stated that his criminal conviction must be considered null and void and ordered his immediate release. Unfortunately, this may not happen. 

Türkiye has already defied two previous binding rulings from the court in his case. And despite pressure from governments, international institutions and campaigners – Amnesty International declared Kavala and his six co-defendants prisoners of conscience in 2022 – Turkish authorities have continued to flagrantly obstruct justice, with very little consequence.
snippet: This week the Grand Chamber of the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) delivered a landmark judgment in the case of prominent Turkish human rights defender, Osman Kavala.

title: Inside the Warehouse Where Amazon Scans and Destroys Books for AI Training
content:
Last week we published a story that revealed an Amazon warehouse where the company scans and destroys thousands of books for AI training data. The following is an interview with one of the Amazon employees at this warehouse. We granted this employee anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to the press. 

The employee worked at Amazon’s VGT3 warehouse, which is housed in the same facility as LAS8, where Amazon operates its print-on-demand business. Both operations are part of a larger complex of Amazon facilities in Las Vegas, Nevada. 

We discovered that VGT3 was used to destructively scan books for AI training data by placing a tracking device in a shipment of rare books that a bookseller suspected was being acquired by an anonymous AI company. We saw the shipment travel across the country before finally landing at VGT3. Online, Amazon employees who worked at VGT3 described the work of receiving shipments of books, cutting the spines off of them, and scanning the loose pages. 

The Amazon employee I talked to described what that operation looks like from the warehouse floor. 

This interview has been edited for clarity and length.

title: How the ‘backwoods Barbie’ Dolly Parton turned self-aware artifice into authentic artistry
content:
Scrolling through the tributes to Dolly Parton this morning – from the Grand Ole Opry, New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, queerfluencers and others – I thought to myself: that’s her real name?

Yes. The “Queen of Country”, who died overnight aged 80, was born Dolly Rebecca Parton. My surprise at the authenticity of her name says something about the contradiction within the figure of Dolly.

A sometime figure of ridicule and satire, the opening image of Dolly – in interviews, send ups and even her own branding – was often related to her apparent “fakeness”.

Her literal figure – breasts, face, hair – was obviously artificial. And often these synthetic additions to her body were transposed into an assumption she herself was, if not inauthentic, at least somewhat superficial. Dolly’s first hit on the country charts was Dumb Blonde in 1967.

But what a name! Not a diminutive of a serious name, not a stage name, but a real name that moves us towards her celebrity image as one: dressed-up, made-up, an object with which the entertainment industry played.

title: How Learning About Capital Letters Brought Wikipedia Into My Classroom
content:
On August 19, 2026, I taught my Bahasa Indonesia class a lesson on capital letters, huruf kapital. On paper, it was an ordinary grammar lesson. For me, it was something I had been waiting for since long before I ever stood in front of a classroom.

I am a Wikimedian and an elementary school teacher from Indonesia. I have spent years believing in this movement, in free knowledge, in the idea that anyone can edit and anyone can learn. But for just as long, I have carried a quiet worry, that Wikipedia’s impact, for all its scale, often stays trapped inside the internet. It’s everywhere, and yet at the grassroots level, in a classroom, in a small village, in the hands of a child, it can still feel invisible. This year, as a brand-new teacher, I finally had a chance to close that gap myself.

title: Vholume review – a headlong rush of parkour perfection in a brutalist wonderland
content:
PC; Nathan Grange, Léonard Lemaitre, Niels Tiercelin, IronEqual
Race across impossible dystopian cityscapes in this exhilarating game of wall-runs, death-chancing leaps and split-second improvisation

At first, Vholume seems like a quick rush through some smartly selected references. Has this breathless yet austere parkour game been designed or ingeniously curated? The urban gymnast moveset comes from Mirror’s Edge. Level names use terms like conapt, first coined by Philip K Dick. And the environments themselves are dystopian and surreal, Half-Life 2’s City 17 colliding with the blasted avenues and mute archways of de Chirico. Many games have influences. Vholume has actual taste.

title: Kuwait: Counterterrorism measures introduced amid Iran war endanger fundamental rights, expand death penalty
content:
A counterterrorism law enacted in Kuwait in the wake of Iranian strikes on the Gulf, following the unlawful US-Israeli attacks on Iran, contains overly broad and vague provisions that threaten the rights to freedom of expression, peaceful assembly, association and movement, while significantly expanding the scope of the death penalty, Amnesty International said today. 

On 15 March 2026, the Emir of Kuwait issued Decree-Law No. 47 of 2026 on Combating Terrorism Crimes, which adopts an overly broad and vague definition of ‘terrorist’ acts. The counterterrorism law forms part of a sweeping package of legal and judicial measures introduced in March 2026 shortly after the Iran war began in the name of “countering terrorism”. Measures include the establishment of a specialized prosecution branch and specially designated courts for terrorism-related charges, as well as significantly expanding the scope of the death penalty for “terrorist acts.”  

National security must not be used as a justification to trample on rights and expand state powers, and responding to any legitimate threats must be pursued in a manner consistent with international law.

Mahmoud Shalaby, Amnesty International

content:
According to HRANA, the news agency of Human Rights Activists in Iran, two prisoners were executed at Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj.

HRANA has confirmed the identities of the two prisoners, who were hanged yesterday, Tuesday, August 25, as Saeed Najafi and Hamid Najafi, two brothers.

According to information received by HRANA, the two brothers were arrested two years ago. They were subsequently sentenced to death by a Revolutionary Court in a joint case on the charge of moharebeh (enmity against God) through armed robbery.

As of the time of this report, the executions of these two prisoners have not been officially announced by prison authorities or other relevant institutions.

title: CBrio: growing knowledge from chemical gardens
content:
“If you have a garden and a library, you have everything you need.”

This famous quote by Cicero reminds us that the beauty of life lies in the harmony between nature and knowledge. More than two thousand years later, this idea still resonates, particularly with a group of European researchers who have created a unique type of ‘garden’: one that grows from chemistry itself.

When certain metal salts are placed in water, strange, delicate, plant-like tubes and filaments begin to grow, twisting and blooming into colourful shapes. These creations, known as chemical gardens, are the result of natural chemical reactions. What appears to be art is actually science in motion.

Behind these mesmerising shapes lies a complex world of physics, chemistry and biology. Understanding these reactions could help scientists to design new materials, improve biomedical devices, capture gases such as carbon dioxide and even gain insight into how life first emerged on Earth.

title: Xamkille laatuleima – vahvuuksina strateginen TKI-toiminta, työelämäyhteistyö ja jatkuva oppiminen
content:
Kaakkois-Suomen ammattikorkeakoulu (Xamk) on läpäissyt Kansallisen koulutuksen arviointikeskuksen (Karvi) auditoinnin. Xamk toimi toisena pilottikorkeakouluna neljännen kierroksen auditointimallissa. Auditointiryhmä arvosti Xamkin strategisesti hyvin johdettua tutkimus-, kehittämis- ja innovaatiotoimintaa (TKI), vahvaa työelämäyhteistyötä sekä jatkuvan oppimisen järjestelmällistä kehittämistä. Auditointiryhmä edellyttää korkeakoululta koulutusohjelmien säännöllisten arviointien aloittamista.

Strateginen TKI-toiminta ja alueellinen vaikuttavuus ovat Xamkin vahvuuksia

Auditointiryhmä nosti TKI-toiminnan ja sen johtamisen Xamkin erityiseksi vahvuudeksi. TKI-toimintaa johdetaan systemaattisesti ja tavoitteellisesti osana korkeakoulun strategisia tavoitteita, ja Xamkilla on vahvat edellytykset hyödyntää tietoa toiminnan kehittämisessä ja johtamisessa. Jatkossa Xamkin on mahdollista vahvistaa entisestään koulutuksen ja TKI-toiminnan välistä yhteyttä ja tehdä TKI-toiminnan vaikutukset koulutukseen nykyistä näkyvämmiksi.

title: AI-kahvit: Näin rakennat oman tekoälyagentin
content:
Tämä Teams-tallenne on osa AI-kahvit-sarjaa, jonka on tuottanut Yleisten kirjastojen tekoälyosaamisen kehittämishanke. AI-kahveilla tutustutaan tällä kertaa käytännönläheisesti niin sanottuihin kevytagentteihin: mitä ne ovat, miten ne eroavat tavallisesta keskustelukäytöstä ja miten oman agentin voi rakentaa vaihe vaiheelta.

Aiheesta puhuu Pinja Valkonen Deeplestä. Hän johdattaa osallistujat konkreettisen esimerkin kautta agentin rakentamiseen Microsoft Copilot Chatissa: tilaisuudessa tehdään yhdessä nuortenkirjoja etsivä agentti, jonka avulla havainnollistetaan, miten agentille annetaan ohjeet, tietolähteet ja vastauksen muoto kerralla talteen, jolloin samaa kehotetta ei tarvitse kirjoittaa aina uudelleen. Valkonen käsittelee myös lyhyesti EU:n tekoälyasetuksen läpinäkyvyysvaatimuksia sekä tekoälyn ympäristövaikutuksia suhteessa muihin arjen valintoihin. Metodiikka on samankaltainen myös muissa yleisimmissä tekoälysovelluksissa (esim. ChatGPT:n Custom GPT:t, Geminin Gems ja Cloudin Projects). Webinaari järjestettiin 25.8.2026.

content:
Alla inbjudna deltar i SI:s internationella ledarskapsprogram, som inom ramen för regeringens internationella strategier bygger långsiktiga relationer mellan svenska aktörer och nyckelpersoner från strategiskt viktiga marknader i exempelvis Indien, Brasilien och Ukraina. 

Programmen för samman internationell och svensk expertis inom digitalisering, innovation och grön omställning – områden där Sverige har stark kompetens.

År 2025 uppgav 44 procent av deltagarna i SI Global Executive Programme att de utforskade konkreta affärsmöjligheter som uppstått genom programmet.

I Impact Pioneers bedömde 96 procent att programmet skapar goda förutsättningar för fortsatta samarbeten, bland annat med svenska företag.

Årets deltagare arbetar bland annat inom hållbara städer, förnybar energi, cirkulär ekonomi, jordbruksteknik, mobilitet och digitalisering.

Svenska institutets nätverksträffar arrangeras i samarbete med Team Sweden – ett nätverk av myndigheter och företag som arbetar tillsammans för att främja svensk export och investeringar i Sverige. Läs mer om Svenska institutets arbete med Team Sweden här.

title: Spotlight on WG DHwiki: Collaborative approaches to sustainable, community‑driven Open Knowledge Infrastructures
content:
DARIAH is delighted to publish the latest Spotlight article WG DHwiki: Collaborative approaches to sustainable, community‑driven Open Knowledge Infrastructures. This article is part of the DARIAH Spotlight campaign, a monthly series that focuses on digital scholarship within the DARIAH network.

Written by members of the DHwiki WG, this article presents the aims and first activities of this WG since its launch in November 2024.

In a short time, DHwiki has grown from a shared interest into a collaborative group with a clear purpose. What started as a process of getting to know one another’s work and experience is gradually becoming a more stable effort to support a wider community of practice. By building connections between research, GLAM, and Wikimedia communities, the Working Group aims to strengthen the role of open and collaborative LOD infrastructures in Digital Humanities.

title: The Wisdom of David Bowie: On Art, Religion, Technology and More
content:
It doesn’t quite ring true to call David Bowie a rock star. Ziggy Stardust, the neon synthetic-clad alien alter ego he both created and retired in the early seventies, was, of course, rock stardom outlandishly personified. But then, that was the concept of what turned out to be just one of many personae he deliberately crafted throughout the course of his career. That career was in music, primarily, but looking back on it today, more than a decade after Bowie’s death, it looks more like his medium was culture itself. That’s underscored by his interviews, clips from a variety of which appear in the new video above from YouTube channel T&H Inspiration.

Most of T&H’s most popular videos add visuals to speeches by the popularizer of Eastern philosophy Alan Watts, who’s been featured here on Open Culture before. He and Bowie had more in common than it may seem at first, beginning with an Englishness that remained thoroughgoing no matter how far out they ventured into the world.

title: Preserving a Creative Legacy: How CARTA is Safeguarding Artists’ Websites
content: Artists today use their websites as more than a business card– they are an online portfolio, CV, document of artistic evolution, and works of art in their own right. They are valuable records of a life’s work, yet as with all technology, they are fragile and ephemeral. They can vanish overnight due to expiring domain registrations, server migrations, software obsolescence, or administrative access loss after the passing of an artist.

title: When Boxing Gloves Meet Museum Walls
content:
There is often a wide gulf between culture lovers and sports enthusiasts. In Antwerp, a hyperdiverse city where martial arts of every kind are widely practised, many practitioners have never set foot in a museum, and plenty of museum regulars have never set foot in a boxing gym. At MuseumNext, three speakers from the city explained how an exhibition is starting to bridge that divide.

Hélène De Pagie, a programme maker at the MAS (Museum aan de Stroom), was joined on stage by Rachid Atia of the Heritage Lab and Jamal Touala of Sporting A, the city’s sports department. Together they told the story of the Martial Arts exhibition, which has brought fighters, wrestlers and boxers into one of Antwerp’s most prestigious cultural spaces, and museum visitors into a world many of them had never given much thought.

title: NATO’s Missing Link: Shielding Vulnerable Infrastructure
content:
A new railway is not a strategic capability if it ends at a vulnerable bridge. A battery is not a reserve if it relies on the substation whose loss it is meant to bridge. A second data center is not redundancy if both sites share a fiber route, supplier, or control layer. Such assets do not necessarily create strategic capability.

Recent US intelligence assessments reportedly warn that Russia may test NATO’s resolve between next month and 2029. NATO must be sure that the civilian infrastructure its forces depend on will work under pressure.

At the 2025 Hague Summit, allies agreed that up to 1.5% of GDP (of the total defense spending pledge of 5%) may include key national infrastructure and resilience. NATO has since approved a €27bn ($32bn) plan for improved fuel storage and distribution, for example, while the European Commission estimates that electricity grids need more than €1.2 trillion by 2040.

title: Nigel Farage wants to scrap GDPR for the UK
content:
LONDON — Reform UK on Tuesday night outlined plans to scrap the U.K.’s data protection regime as part of a broader package of measures designed to help small businesses.

The U.K. decided to incorporate an amended version of the EU’s General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) privacy laws into British law post-Brexit. Reform UK says it would replace the U.K. version of GDPR with a “light-touch” privacy law modeled on New Zealand’s approach to data protection.

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said small businesses have had to deal with “suffocating EU red tape” and the package, which includes abolishing GDPR, is a “bold, common-sense rescue plan.”

“[T]he GDPR has strangled small businesses and tech firms alike in a web of unnecessary regulation … Ten years after the Brexit referendum we should not still be following ridiculous EU privacy laws that hurt British businesses,” Reform UK MP Robert Jenrick said in a statement.  

The EU GDPR provides for a wider set of individual rights around personal data (including the “right to be forgotten”) than New Zealand’s Privacy Act does.

title: Türkiye: Osman Kavala must be immediately released following European Court order to quash his conviction
content:
The Grand Chamber of the European Court of Human Rights today delivered a landmark judgment in the case of Osman Kavala, the human rights defender and civil society leader unlawfully imprisoned in Türkiye since November 2017. The Court ruled that Kavala’s continued detention is unlawful and found that his rights to fair trial, freedom of expression and association have been violated. The Court also found that his aggravated life sentence amounts to inhuman and degrading treatment and that the Turkish authorities acted in bad faith by keeping him in detention unlawfully. The Court concluded that he was convicted for the ulterior purpose of punishing and silencing him, and to prevent his human rights work. The Court ordered his release at the earliest possible date and that his conviction be quashed. 

Human rights organisations Human Rights Watch, International Commission of Jurists, and the Turkey Litigation Support Project submitted a joint intervention to the Court on the core rights issues at stake in the case. Amnesty International declared Osman Kavala and his six co-defendants prisoners of conscience in June 2022.
