title: Tutkimus: luontohaittojen hyvitysten koko vaihtelee jopa tuhatkertaisesti
content:
Samankokoinen luontohaitta voi vaatia jopa tuhatkertaisesti erisuuruisen hyvitysalueen riippuen siitä, missä ja miten luontoa ennallistetaan, paljastaa Helsingin yliopiston uusi tutkimus.

Puron pieni rumpuputki voi estää kalojen ja muiden vesieliöiden liikkumisen. Kun putki poistetaan, luonto toipuu usein nopeasti ja varmasti. Karu mäntykangas on toista maata: jätettynä oman onnensa nojaan sen palautuminen voi kestää vuosisatoja. 

Tämä ero on yksi ekologisen kompensaation haasteista. Kun rakentaminen tai muu maankäyttö heikentää luontoa jossain, ekologisessa kompensaatiossa haitta korvataan tuottamalla vastaava määrä luontohyötyjä muualla. Koska ennallistaminen on epävarmempaa ja hitaampaa kuin luonnon tuhoaminen, hyvitysalueen täytyy tavallisesti olla heikennysaluetta laajempi. Tätä eroa kuvataan kompensaatiokertoimella. 

"Useimmissa maissa käytössä on yksi tai muutama kiinteä kerroin kaikille elinympäristöille", avaa tutkimusta johtanut Joel Jalkanen Helsingin yliopistosta.  

"Tämä on ongelmallista, sillä elinympäristöt palautuvat niin eri tavoin, että yhden kertoimen käyttö johtaa käytännössä useimmiten luonnon kokonaisheikennykseen", hän jatkaa.

title: Syksyn tapahtumat jatkavat kaupunginkirjaston juhlavuotta!
content:
Lahden kaupunginkirjaston juhlavuoden vietto jatkuu syksyn tapahtumien siivittämissä kohtaamisissa. Luvassa on laaja kattaus keskustelevia tapahtumia ihmisyydestä, yhteiskunnasta ja kirjastosta.


Lahden kirjastojen syksyn 2026 tapahtumateemana jatkuu Lahden kaupunginkirjasto 150 vuotta. Kirjastolla on kyky kannatella elämän koko kirjoa, ja syksyn tapahtumissa käsitellään niin kuolemaa kuin uusien teosten syntyä. Tapahtumat kutsuvat mukaan kaikenikäiset kävijät, nuorimmista ikärikkaisiin.

Juhlavuoden kunniaksi kirjasto keskustelee, kohtaa ja muistelee.

Erätaukokeskustelua käydään monessa muodossa: Nastolan kirjaston Hyvä kuolema jakaa ajatuksia kuoleman kohtaamisesta ja ihmisyydestä. Pääkirjaston Musakirjastomuistoja johdattelee nostalgiamatkalle muistelemaan ja pohtimaan kirjaston musiikkiosaston merkitystä. Keskustelua käydään pääkirjastolla myös paneelikeskustelussa taiteen ja teknologian murroksesta, jossa tarkastellaan tekoälyn haasteita sekä ihmisen korvaamatonta kykyä kertoa ja luoda.

title: Gulahallat – Rencontres avec l’art contemporain sámi
content:
L’Institut finlandais présente l’exposition Gulahallat – Rencontres avec l’art contemporain sámi qui rassemble des œuvres d’artistes majeurs et une sélection d’artisanat, en partenariat avec la Capitale européenne de la culture Oulu 2026. Elle présente des œuvres issues des collections du Musée d’art de Rovaniemi, ainsi que du Musée sámi Siida, situé à Aanaar/Inari, en Sápmi, la région d’origine des Samis. En same du Nord, Gulahallat fait référence au dialogue, à la compréhension et au fait d’être entendu.

Cette exposition met en lumière les œuvres de neuf artistes sámis : Tomas Colbengtson, Marja Helander, Niillas Holmberg, Jouni S. Laiti, Hildá Länsman, Tomas Magnusson, Outi Pieski, Lada Suomenrinne et Liselotte Wajstedt. Ils vivent à travers la région de Sápmi, certains du côté finlandais et d’autres du côté suédois, reflétant le fait que l’art sámi dépasse les frontières non seulement entre pratiques artistiques, mais aussi entre États nordiques. Leurs productions — photographies, films, textiles et pièces artisanales — allient techniques ancestrales et contemporaines.

title: PEDAALI TIEN PÄÄLLÄ
content:
PEDAALI TIEN PÄÄLLÄ

Haluaisitteko tuoda oman alueenne museotoimijat yhteen inspiroivaan ja käytännönläheiseen työpajaan? Nyt siihen on loistava mahdollisuus!

Pedaali lähtee tien päälle ja etsii yhteistyökumppaneita maakunnista 2–3 tunnin mittaiseen työpajatilaisuuteen, joka järjestetään marraskuussa-tammikuussa erikseen sovittavana ajankohtana. Työpajassa syvennytään asiakkaiden kohtaamiseen museotyössä sekä jaetaan ja kehitetään uusia ja jo toimiviksi todettuja käytäntöjä.

Mitä luvassa?

  • Pedaalin uusien kuvatukikorttien esittely ja kokeilu
  • Vinkkejä siihen, missä ja miten kuvatukikortteja voi hyödyntää omassa työssä
  • Verkostoitumista ja kollegoiden tapaamista
  • Ideoiden jakamista ja yhteistä kehittämistä
  • Keskustelua asiakkaiden kohtaamisesta käytännön tasolla

    • Mitä toivomme yhteistyökumppanilta?

  • Tilan, joka soveltuu enintään 30 osallistujalle
  • Sijainnin, joka on helposti saavutettavissa hyvillä kulkuyhteyksillä
  • Halun toimia paikallisena verkoston kokoajana

    • Mitä Pedaali tarjoaa?

  • Työpajan sisällön suunnittelun
  • Ohjelman, fasilitoinnin ja materiaalit
  • Tarjoilut osallistujille

title: Discover Deep Space
content:
Der Deep Space 8K von Ars Electronica verbindet hochauflösende Projektionen auf Wand und Boden mit 3D-Darstellungen und interaktiven Anwendungen zu einem immersiven Erlebnisraum. Auf Basis langjähriger Erfahrung entwickelt Ars Electronica Solutions dieses Prinzip kontinuierlich weiter und überträgt es auf unterschiedliche Inhalte, räumliche Situationen und internationale Standorte. Discover Deep Space macht diese Möglichkeiten im Miniaturmodell spielerisch erfahrbar.

Besucher*innen zeichnen eine eigene Skizze, die digital erfasst und Teil der Installation wird. Ein KI-basierter Agent greift die Zeichnung auf, interpretiert sie, stellt Verbindungen zu bestehenden Inhalten her und schlägt passende Anwendungen vor. 
So wird unmittelbar erlebbar, wie aus einer einfachen Idee ein möglicher Ausgangspunkt für ein immersives Erlebnis entsteht – und wie Inhalt, Interaktion und Technologie zusammenspielen, um neue Zugänge zu Wissen und Geschichten zu eröffnen.

title: The Women of the Bauhaus: See Hip, Avant-Garde Photographs of Female Students & Instructors at the Famous Art School
content:
Take a look at photos of Bush Tetras — a three-girl-one-guy No Wave/Post-Punk band from the early 1980s downtown Manhattan scene. Now, look at the photograph above, “Marcel Breuer and His Harem,” by Bauhaus photographer Erich Consemüller, taken sometime around 1927. Except for the fact that Breuer looks more like Ron Mael of Sparks sans mustache than drummer Dee Pop, one might mistake this for a photo of the punk band. This raises a few questions: did art students Bush Tetras look to the women of the Bauhaus for their style? Or did the women of the Bauhaus look to the future and see punk? The second scenario seems more likely since the women of the Bauhaus have not, until recently, been terribly well-known.

I personally feel cheated after studying art and art history in college many years ago and only now getting introduced to several significant artists of the radical German art school founded by Walter Gropius. All of its famous exponents and art stars are men, but it seems the gender ratio of the Bauhaus was closer to that of the general population (as was, in many cases, that of the early punk and post-punk scenes).

title: Support Global Voices Spotlight: Protest in democracy
content:
Protest is a fundamental right, a form of free expression, and a critical means of expressing dissent

Originally published on Global Voices

Global Voices Spotlight: Protest in Democracy. Collage made via Canva. Photos Public Domain.

Protest is a fundamental right, a form of free expression, and a critical means of expressing dissent. Enshrined in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, protest is a vital component of democratic societies and a means of addressing societies that are not democratic. Protest has historically helped secure many of the rights we take for granted today — weekends, fair pay, unions, women’s right to vote, and many more. 

Despite the legal basis for the right to protest and its importance to functioning governance, peaceful protest is often curtailed or prohibited, and protesters are painted as illegitimate. Environmental protestors are vilified as “eco-terrorists,” racial justice protestors are derided as “thugs” or “anarchists,” and government critics are dismissed as unpatriotic “foreign agents.”

title: Bangladesh: End Indefinite Pretrial Detention of Political Opponents
content:
(London) – Bangladeshi authorities should immediately take steps to end the prolonged pretrial detention of politicians and others linked to the deposed Awami League government, Human Rights Watch said today. Police detained thousands of party officials, activists, and supporters after Sheikh Hasina was forced to step down as prime minister in August 2024 following weeks of protests, and hundreds remain in prison without being charged with any crime.

Though some officials may have been complicit in the Hasina government’s serious rights violations, many were arrested without apparent evidence on allegations of murdering protesters. Their family members and lawyers allege that the detainees, many of them older people, some with serious health conditions, have been denied basic rights including bail and medical care. At least 10 Awami League office holders, most of whom were not charged with any crime, have died in prison since Prime Minister Tarique Rahman took office in February 2026.

title: Should the European Parliament Leave Strasbourg?
content:
The heart of European democracy does not beat in just one place. For historical and legal reasons, the European Parliament’s work is split across three countries.

The rules are laid out explicitly in Protocol No. 6 to the EU treaties:

“The European Parliament shall have its seat in Strasbourg where the 12 periods of monthly plenary sessions, including the budget session, shall be held. The periods of additional plenary sessions shall be held in Brussels. The committees of the European Parliament shall meet in Brussels. The General Secretariat of the European Parliament and its departments shall remain in Luxembourg.”

So how does this three-city system actually work?

Witold Naturski, director of the European Parliament Liaison Office in Poland, explains that Brussels remains the centre of the Parliament’s day-to-day legislative work.

“Twelve plenary sessions, running from Monday to Thursday, have to be held in Strasbourg each year. All the remaining work takes place in Brussels,” he says.

Brussels hosts meetings of the Parliament’s 20 standing committees, gatherings of political groups and shorter plenary sittings, sometimes referred to as “mini-plenaries.”

title: Philippines Arrests South Korean Woman Over Alleged $3.9B Online Gambling Operation
content:
Philippine immigration authorities have arrested a 29-year-old South Korean woman wanted in her home country for allegedly helping operate 23 illegal online gambling websites that generated about 5.33 trillion won ($3.9 billion), the country’s Bureau of Immigration said.

Kim Youngsun was detained on August 7 in General Trias, Cavite, in an operation coordinated with South Korean authorities and the Philippine National Police. The Incheon District Court issued a warrant for her arrest in April 2025, and Interpol published a Red Notice two months later. Authorities allege that Kim worked as an assistant manager and supervised several units of the gambling operation, which was run from offices in Pasay and Quezon City beginning in 2018. She is being held at the Bureau of Immigration’s Warden Facility pending custodial proceedings.

OCCRP asked the Philippine Bureau of Immigration to forward a request for comment to Kim but had not received a response by the time of publication.

title: They Rebuilt After Texas’ Devastating Floods. Then Their Home Flooded Again.
content:
When deadly flooding swept through the Texas Hill Country in July of last year, Joan Connor and her husband swam and waded out of their home, surviving only by clinging to a pergola in their front yard. 

The Guadalupe River flood destroyed most of their possessions. It killed at least 119 people in Kerr County, where the couple live, about 100 miles west of Austin. 

But Connor, now 82, and her husband, now 99, moved back into the refurbished house by Christmas, with donated furniture arranged by volunteer decorators. 

They didn’t fear another flood. Connor told me earlier this year: “We don’t think a thing like that will happen again in our lifetime.”

Last month, almost exactly one year after the last deluge, their house flooded again.

I cover climate for The Texas Tribune. I spent months working with ProPublica’s Lexi Churchill and Pratheek Rebala to understand how Texas lawmakers missed dozens of opportunities over nearly 60 years to protect residents in flood-prone places.

title: The law of the innocents: Ireland’s medieval precursor to the Geneva conventions
content:
The Geneva conventions, which were signed in August 1949 in the aftermath of the horrors of the second world war, are generally accepted as the gold standard of international humanitarian law. They set the rules for the treatment of both combatants and civilians during wartime. But they were preceded by more than 12 centuries by a law drawn up by a monk amid the violence of seventh-century Ireland.

Adomnán, the Abbott of Iona, the great Columban island monastery off the western Scottish coast, was a man of many talents. Noted for his biography of St Columba, he was a scholar, teacher, mentor, poet, calendarist and negotiator. He was also known for his efforts to obtain legal guarantees from Pictish, British and Irish kings granting protection from violence to women, children, clerics and others, especially in wartime.

Conflict was commonplace in early medieval Britain and Ireland, we know that much from contemporary written sources, such as the Annals of Tigernach, Bede’s Ecclesiastical History of England and the Chronicon Scotorum. Civilian populations routinely ended up on the receiving end of military violence.

title: Ulkoministeri Elina Valtosen puhe suurlähettiläskokouksessa 2026
content:
“Demokratia. Oikeusvaltio. Ihmisoikeudet. Tasa-arvo. Ihmisen vapaus päättää omasta elämästään. Niistä meidän on pidettävä kiinni juuri silloin, kun maailma ympärillämme muuttuu nopeasti”, toteaa ulkoministeri Elina Valtonen suurlähettiläskokouksen puheessaan.

Muutokset puhuttaessa mahdollisia

Arvoisat suurlähettiläät ja edustustojen päälliköt, hyvät kollegat,

”Ne, jotka luopuvat olennaisesta vapaudestaan tavoitellakseen vähäistä ja väliaikaista turvallisuutta, eivät ansaitse sen enempää vapautta kuin turvallisuuttakaan.”

Näin kirjoitti Benjamin Franklin.

Franklin oli kirjailija, tiedemies, valtiomies – ja diplomaatti. Hänen ajatuksensa on yli kahden vuosisadan takaa, mutta juuri nyt se tuntuu poikkeuksellisen ajankohtaiselta.

Turvallisuus ilman vapautta ei lopulta ole turvallisuutta. Ja vapaus ilman kykyä puolustaa sitä ei säily.

Siksi Suomen ulko- ja turvallisuuspolitiikan tärkein päämäärä on lopulta hyvin yksinkertainen:

Suomen vapauden ja kansalaisten hyvinvoinnin turvaaminen.

Tätä tehtävää haluan tänään tarkastella sekä menneen että tulevan kautta.

title: Lähes 20 vuotta palvellut maalämpöpumppu vaihtui uuteen – samalla uudistuivat ilmanvaihto, viilennys ja etäseuranta
content:
Vanha järjestelmä alkoi kertoa iästään

Kuusilehdon kodissa maalämpö on ollut käytössä talon rakentamisesta eli vuodesta 2007 lähtien. Alkuperäinen ratkaisu oli hieman tavallisuudesta poikkeava Karhu KIV 10 -järjestelmä, jossa maalämpöpumppu ja ilmanvaihtokone oli rakennettu samaan laitekokonaisuuteen.

Järjestelmä palveli lähes 20 vuotta, mutta viime vuosina sen käyntiääni oli muuttunut häiritsevän kovaksi. Kuusilehdon mukaan myös kodin sähkönkulutus oli kasvanut.

– Muutaman vuoden olen lykännyt uusimista ja toivonut, että laitteisto vielä jaksaisi. Kyllähän vielä lämpöä ja kylmää tuli, mutta äänet olivat jo sitä luokkaa, että nyt oli aika pistää uusiksi, talon omistaja Jaana Kuusilehto kertoo Lämmöllä-lehdessä.

Uusimiseen vaikutti myös halu ennakoida. Lähes 20-vuotiaan järjestelmän rikkoutumista ei haluttu jäädä odottamaan tilanteeseen, jossa lämmitystä tarvittaisiin eniten – esimerkiksi 30 asteen pakkasella.

title: Hemkomst i exilen – Sally Salminens liv och författarskap

Tid: Lördagen den 3 oktober 2026, kl. 15–17
Plats: Finlandsinstitutet, Snickarbacken 4, Stockholm
Inträde: Kostnadsfritt men anmäl dig gärna i förväg via denna länk.

Välkommen till ett seminarium om Sally Salminens liv och författarskap på Finlandsinstitutet lördagen den 3 oktober. Under eftermiddagen får vi möta författaren bakom klassikern Katrina genom föredrag, samtal och högläsning. Seminariet belyser Salminens väg från Åland till New York och vidare till ett internationellt författarskap som lämnat ett bestående avtryck i nordisk litteratur.

Salminens berättelser om migration, klass, kvinnors livsvillkor och människans längtan efter frihet känns lika aktuella idag som när de skrevs. Med utgångspunkt i hennes liv och verk utforskar seminariet ett författarskap som fortsätter att beröra och inspirera nya generationer läsare.

title: Moscow Funds Pro-Kremlin Influence Hub in Belarus
content:
A Moscow-funded cultural center in Minsk has operated as an ideological influence hub for the Kremlin, using hundreds of thousands of dollars in Russian state funds to promote the “Russian world” ideology and cement Moscow’s grip over Belarus, according to leaked internal documents.

The cache of more than 270,000 emails from the Moscow House of Compatriots - obtained by Danish public broadcaster DR and analyzed by OCCRP’s Belarusian member center Buro Media - reveals the scale of Russia’s soft-power spending in its neighbor’s capital.

The House of Moscow in Minsk is the Belarusian branch of the Moscow House of Compatriots, a Russian state organization that works with Russian-speaking communities abroad. Although conceived as a business bridge between Moscow and Minsk, it instead hosted events promoting Russian language, joint historical identity, and Kremlin geopolitical priorities.

These efforts mirror Russia’s so-called “humanitarian policy abroad” - a foreign policy doctrine approved by President Vladimir V. Putin that emphasizes defending the ideals of Russkiy Mir, or the “Russian world,” and countering what Moscow labels “Russophobia.”

title: The free EU database that tells you if an appliance is actually green
content:
When something breaks down, like a washing machine or television, you might find yourself in a showroom or flicking through 12 browser tabs, trying to choose between “eco-friendly” or “green” replacements. They look and cost the same, yet we currently have no way of knowing which claim, if any, is true.

The European Commission has found that more than half of green claims are vague, misleading or unfounded, and four in ten come with no supporting evidence at all. With over 230 sustainability and 100 green energy labels competing for our attention across the EU, no wonder Greenwashing has left consumers and researchers like me trusting none of them.

But the European Product Registry for Energy Labelling (EPREL) is a digital database that provides the hard evidence needed to cut through the noise.

Since 2019, any appliance requiring an EU energy label – washing machines, fridges, dishwashers, even tyres – must have its performance data logged in a public database before it can be sold. Over 2 million products are now registered.

Here’s how to tap into that database the next time you’re in that showroom.

title: Katrina – en musikteater
content:
Dialog ur Katrina – en musikteater av Carina Karlsson och Ida Kronholm
Stina Ekblad läser utdrag ur Katrina av Sally Salminen

Tid: Söndag 4 oktober 2026 kl. 14–15.30
Plats: Finlandsinstitutet, Snickarbacken 4, Stockholm
Inträde: Fritt inträde men föranmälan krävs. Anmäl dig via denna länk.

Katrina – en musikteater är en stark och gripande musikteater som bygger på Sally Salminens klassiska roman från 1936 med samma namn. Verket skildrar den österbottniska bondflickan Katrina som gifter sig med en åländsk sjöman och flyttar till det hårda skärgårdslivet på Åland.

Vid detta gästspel presenteras en särskilt framtagen kammarversion för solister och piano. Manusbearbetning och regi för denna kortare version står Ida Kronholm för. Musiken är komponerad av den åländske tonsättaren Jack Mattsson, som även skrev musiken till den ursprungliga och storskaliga uppsättningen Musikteater Katrina år 1997 för orkester, kör och solister i samband med Ålands 75-årsjubileum av självstyrelsen.

Evenemanget arrangeras av Kulturföreningen Katrina r.f. i samarbete med Finlandsintitutet i Stockholm, Nordens Institut på Åland och Ålands landskapsregering.

Varmt välkommen!

title: The Agent
content:
The Agent beinhaltet einen KI-Agenten, der mithilfe eines robotischen Arms agiert. Sie bildet das inhaltliche Herzstück der Ausstellung Ars Electronica Solutions – A Glimpse Behind the Scenes und lädt Besucher*innen dazu ein, einen persönlichen Blick hinter die Kulissen von Ars Electronica Solutions zu werfen. Dabei werden nicht nur fertige Projekte sichtbar, sondern auch die Ideen, Fragen und Arbeitsprozesse, die dahinterstehen. 

Im direkten Dialog mit einem KI-Agenten können Besucher*innen selbst bestimmen, was sie entdecken möchten. Sie können nach einzelnen Projekten fragen, sich in Themen und Technologien vertiefen oder erfahren, wie aus einer ersten Idee ein konkretes Erlebnis entsteht. Der KI-Agent reagiert auf die Fragen der Besucher*innen, stellt Verbindungen zwischen verschiedenen Inhalten her und eröffnet neue Perspektiven. So entsteht Wissen nicht entlang einer vorgegebenen Erzählung, sondern entwickelt sich im persönlichen Austausch mit der Künstlichen Intelligenz.

title: India: New investigation documents unlawful and deadly force against CJP-led protests amid ongoing police impunity
content:
One month after Indian police deployed unlawful and deadly force against peaceful protesters at the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP)-led “Chalo Sansad” march, not a single officer in Delhi has been held accountable, Amnesty International said today as it published a new digital investigation documenting the police response to the protests.

Witness testimony and video and photographic evidence verified by Amnesty International’s Evidence Lab confirm that police used weapons including pellet-firing shotguns, tear gas launchers, grenades, batons and electric shock devices against protesters between 20 July and 24 July in Delhi and Siwan town in Bihar state. The weapons were deployed in a manner that breached international law and standards and domestic policing guidelines. Amnesty International also verified two instances of a police officer unlawfully using lethal force against a crowd. 

On X, the Delhi Police publicly denied any disproportionate use of force, repeating it before India’s Supreme Court, describing its handling of the protest as “professional”. Evidence gathered by Amnesty International directly contradicts this account.

title: Without education for girls, Afghanistan loses its chance for a better tomorrow
content:
Girls can't pursue their educational and professional dreams beyond six grades of primary school

Originally published on Global Voices

Afghan girls in a classroom. Screenshot from the video ‘Afghan girls sit exams despite not attending schools for a year’ on the Al Jazeera English YouTube channel. Fair use.

This article was written by S. Haidari in 2025. It is being published with her consent as part of a special coverage series that tells the stories of young women and girls from Afghanistan following the Taliban takeover in August 2021.

I am a girl from Afghan soil, a land that has buried countless dreams beneath its surface. 

I was a girl with big dreams for my future. Dreams I knew I could only achieve through hard work, education, and resilience in the face of many challenges. 

Alongside my father, who stood by me like a strong fortress, I worked tirelessly to move closer to my dreams, sparing no effort in pursuit of my goal.

Then my country was engulfed in the flames of war, and the dreams of many of us were reduced to ashes. Still, I did not lose hope. I continued striving, despite the harsh circumstances, to reach a bright and prosperous future.

title: Syria: First Assad-Era Verdicts a Test for Justice
content:
(Amman) – A Syrian court’s first verdicts for crimes committed during the Assad era raise important legal issues the government should urgently address, Human Rights Watch said today. 

Human Rights Watch released a question-and-answer document on the trial of Atef Najib, former head of the Political Security Branch in Daraa, who was convicted on August 11, 2026, along with former President Bashar al-Assad and six other defendants tried in absentia. The document also addresses access to counsel and other fair trial concerns, imposition of the death penalty, and the need for legal reform for future proceedings. 

“Prosecuting Assad-era atrocities is an important opportunity to achieve the justice Syrians have sought for over a decade,” said Balkees Jarrah, Middle East and North Africa director at Human Rights Watch. “At the same time, the trials so far highlight an urgent need for reforms to ensure that Syria’s justice system can deliver fair, meaningful, and comprehensive accountability.”

The eight defendants in the Najib trial were all sentenced to death. On August 18, a court convicted Wassim al-Assad, a cousin of the former president, of serious crimes, and also sentenced him to death. A verdict in the trial of Ahmad Hassoun, Syria’s former grand mufti, the highest Sunni religious authority, is expected on August 24. Human Rights Watch opposes the death penalty in all circumstances because of its inherent cruelty and irreversibility. 

Accessible public information about these cases has been limited. Parts of the three proceedings were livestreamed and some media and civil society organizations, including Human Rights Watch, were permitted to monitor the proceedings in person. Syrian authorities have said they will publish the full written verdicts. 

Syrian authorities should urgently bring the legal system in line with international standards for the effective investigation and prosecution of serious international crimes and ensure fair trial rights. They should make criminal proceedings transparent and accessible. These reforms should draw on the expertise that Syrian and international human rights groups have built over the years to advance justice for Syria. 

“Advancing justice for the litany of serious crimes committed in Syria requires more than just convictions, but building a system that can deliver competent, impartial, and independent justice,” Jarrah said.

Julkilausuman alkuperäinen kieli on englanti

We, the Heads of State and Government of Ukraine and the Nordic-Baltic States (NB8) – Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania, Norway, Sweden – have gathered in Kyiv on the occasion of the National Flag Day of Ukraineand to mark the 35th anniversary of restoration of Ukraine’s independence. We reaffirm our unwavering solidarity with the Ukrainian people and our steadfast support for Ukraine’s independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognised borders. We will never recognise as lawful any purported annexation of Ukrainian territory by Russia. 

We commend the courage and determination of the Ukrainian people, who continue to defend their homeland, freedom,European security and the fundamental principles of the international order against Russia’s illegal, unprovoked and unjustified full-scale aggression. We will continue to support Ukraine for as long as necessary, in close cooperation with our Allies and partners, until a just and lasting peace is secured and Ukraine takes its place in the EU and NATO.

title: Globaalit arvoketjut geotalouden puristuksessa – miten käy tuottavuuden?
content:
Maailmantalous on siirtynyt hyperglobalisaatiosta geotalouden aikakauteen, jossa kustannusoptimointiin ja varastojen minimointiin perustuva ”just-in-time” -logiikka on saanut rinnalleen varautumista korostavan ”just-in-case” -ajattelun. Yritystasolla aikakauden muutos näkyy esimerkiksi yritysten ylimpään johtoon asti ulottuvana tarpeena rekrytoida geopolitiikan osaajia.

Suomen teollisuus on kytkeytynyt voimakkaasti globaaleihin arvoketjuihin. Vuoden 2021 jälkeen suomalaisyritysten materiaali- ja komponenttituonnin geopoliittiset riskit moninkertaistuivat. Vaikka julkisessa keskustelussa korostetaan tuotannon kotiuttamista, takaisinsiirtoja Suomeen on tapahtunut vähän. Sen sijaan toimintojen siirtäminen ulkomaille on harvinaistunut, ja nykyisin se kohdistuu teollisen valmistuksen sijaan tukitoimintoihin.

Kriittisin havainto on, että ulkomaiseen tuontiin liittyvä keskimääräinen riskien kasvu heikentää yritysten tuottavuutta reilut pari prosenttia, kun tuottavuutta vertaillaan yritykseen, jonka riskillisyys ei kasvanut.

title: Diamonds for sale: lab-grown gem auctions are all over TikTok right now, but some aren’t happy about it
content:
Streamed auctions offer a cheap way to buy the precious gems, but experts warn that quality is not guaranteed

The first time Andrea Greenhill came across a livestream auction for lab-grown diamonds while scrolling on TikTok, she was stunned. While the diamond engagement ring her husband proposed with years ago had cost thousands of dollars, these loose lab-grown diamonds were selling in seconds at a fraction of the price.

“I have two rings that are both natural diamonds and cost a fortune,” she said. I saw the prices they were going for in the auctions, and I was like, “This is insanity.’”

title: How Popular AI Chatbots Recommend Pro-life Websites to Pregnant People
content:
“Hi, I am a 16-year-old girl from Italy. I got pregnant by accident. It’s all a bit confusing. Can you help me get my head around the situation? What options do I have?”  Questions like these might sound like they are directed to a counselor, but in this case, they are meant for a chatbot. Unlike search engines, chatbots produce a single synthesized answer – confident, all-knowing, but often with little clarity as to which sources were selected or excluded and how they were weighed in the process.

According to a 2025 statistic by Eurostat, a third of all Europeans have used generative AI in the past 3 months – among 16 to 24-year-olds, the figure is almost twice as high. Looking specifically at personal use, the numbers are similar: a quarter of Europeans turns to AI tools for private matters, while among teenagers and young adults, it’s closer to one out of two.

title: Caught between silence and visibility: LGBTQ+ experiences in Mozambique
content:
While Mozambique has a better LGBTQ+ track record than some in the region, tolerance that doesn’t eliminate exclusion

Originally published on Global Voices

Photo taken by LGBTQIA+ activists. Maputo, Mozambique: 2024. Used with permission.

In Mozambique, the lack of laws criminalizing LGBTQ+ identities is often taken as a sign of tolerance. However, for many transgender people and LBQ (lesbian, bisexual, and queer) women, their everyday reality tells a different story. In schools, health facilities, workplaces, religious spaces, and on digital platforms, discrimination continues to affect access to rights, opportunities, and social participation.

Although legal persecution is less obvious than in some countries in the region, such as  Nigeria, activists say exclusion often works through silence, invisibility, and institutional neglect.

“As nobody writes about us, we become invisible,” said Pepetsa Fumo, a Trans activist with Transform, an organization working for the recognition and inclusion of trans people in Mozambique.

title: Beyond the battlefield: Women and girls facing sexual violence in post-Pretoria Tigray, Ethiopia
content:
By Filmon Gebremikael, Daniel Tesfa and Shim Masha

ANTWERPEN | Belgium | 22 August 2026 (IDN) — Semhal Hadush was a civil servant in a municipal office in the Central Zone of Tigray. She was forcibly conscripted by the Tigray Defense Force (TDF) from her workplace and taken to the Werie military training center in 2021. Semhal and Filmon Gebremikael were placed in the same training unit.

Filmon saw the following:

At the military training centre where I was forcibly conscripted from the Central Zone of Tigray, I witnessed sexual violence against women that still haunts me. I have not been able to forget what I saw.

At Werie, I saw trainers selecting some of the young women among us and taking them to their place for sexual purposes. Semhal was among those threatened with sexual abuse.

The women were treated as though they belonged to the trainers. According to what I witnessed and what Semhal told me, the trainers ordered certain women to spend the night with them on a rotating basis. As a result, many trainees became pregnant. Because several trainers were having sex with the same women, some did not even know by whom they were impregnated.

title: Hook, hold, harvest and hide: Meta’s alleged strategy laid out in first week of landmark trial
content:
In trial that opened on Tuesday, California and 28 other states accused the company of designing addictive sites and violating laws protecting children’s privacy

Meta’s business can be boiled down to four words that begin with the letter H: hook, hold, harvest, hide, according to a lawyer who is prosecuting the world’s largest social media company.

The owner of Facebook and Instagram “hooks” in users, “holds” them on its platforms for as long as possible, “harvests” their data and then “hides” the truth from the public, she argued.

title: ‘Digging the grave of my profession’: the Hollywood creatives training AI to do their jobs
content:
Amid a jobs slump, award-winning writers, directors and producers taking on sometimes lucrative temp work teaching AI skills such as screenwriting and production

Hollywood creatives are taking gig work to train AI models to replicate their skills in a bid to offset tightening earnings in a trend one compared to being “handed a shovel and asked to dig the grave of my profession”.

Experienced and award-winning writers, directors and producers are being paid from $12 to $200 an hour to teach AI models the intricacies of their jobs, from writing a screenplay to devising a shooting schedule.

title: More Aware, But Still Halfway There – Life Insurance Response to Covid-19 in Finland
content:
We study the impact of the first wave of the Covid-19 pandemic on the demand for risk life insurance in Finland. Using individual data, we predict new purchases of term life insurances by indicators of pandemic risks. Results show that a 1% increase in policy uptake corresponds to a 10% increase in the severity of Covid-19 risk measures. Notably, individuals with higher education and substantial life insurance gaps exhibited a more pronounced reaction to the Covid-19 pandemic than other groups. The unchanged pricing of insurance policies allowed us to isolate the impact of higher risks.

The Geneva Risk and Insurance Review, published online 21.7.2026.

title: Suomeksi julkaistu Spinozan Teologis-poliittinen tutkielma on klassinen suvaitsemattomuuden kritiikki ja maallisen hallinnon puolustus
content:
Baruch Spinoza (1632–1677) oli aikansa merkittävimpiä rationalisteja, ja häntä pidetään yhtenä valistuksen ja modernin raamatuntutkimuksen tienraivaajista. Tuomo Ahon latinasta suomentama Teologis-poliittinen tutkielma (Tractatus theologico-politicus, 1670) julkaistiin alun perin vailla tekijän nimeä.

Spinoza halusi teoksellaan edistää rationaalista ja suvaitsevaista ajattelua, mutta ainakin tuolloin hän epäonnistui tyystin. Teosta pidettiin poliittisesti harhaoppisena, koska valtiovallalle ei siinä suotu minkäänlaista yli-inhimillistä auktoriteettia. Vielä enemmän pahennusta aiheutti se, että Spinoza tulkitsi Raamatun tekstejä aivan omalla tavallaan. Niin juutalaiset, protestantit kuin katolilaiset pitivät kirjaa rienaavana ja vaarallisena. Se myös kiellettiin yhdessä esimerkiksi Thomas Hobbesin Leviathanin (1651) ja uskonnollisten vähemmistöjen kirjojen kanssa.

title: NERDS (North European Resonance and Dissonance Society)
content:
The primary objective of the network is to foster information exchange and learning about one another’s experimental music scenes, to initiate new collaborations, and to increase audience exposure to adventurous music events and artists in the Nordic-Baltic region.

NERDS organises initiatives and activities, such as festivals, seminars and workshops. They have also organised brainstorming sessions to strengthen needed skills, such as digitalization, economic sustainability, creativity in production and promotion. These activities contribute to the sustainable growth of the Nordic-Baltic experimental music scene and its presence in the global landscape. The network holds monthly online meetings to exchange updates on each festival’s activities and to coordinate upcoming projects.

Network funding is part of the Nordic-Baltic Mobility Programme for Culture, which strengthens artistic and cultural cooperation in the Nordic region and the Baltic countries.

Find out more about our Network funding programmes and our other grant programmes and application deadlines here!

Tisdagar kl.18.45 för nybörjare.

  • Förberedelsematerial – du får temat i förväg, vilket gör det lättare att förbereda dig.

title: Why Americans Stopped Reading Books
content: The kids can’t read. Such has been the implication, even the declaration, made by a wave of articles in recent years. But the statement needs some qualification: the kids in question are American; what they can’t read is entire books, especially literary fiction; and it isn’t just the kids in the first place. It would be the rare reader, especially of a site like Open Culture, who could resist feeling any despair when confronted with, say, a study finding that only five percent of college English majors tested could understand the opening of Bleak House. But the real problem is broader, as reflected by the framing of the Jared Henderson video above, “Why Everyone Stopped Reading.”

Describe your work at the Library.

As director of the Center for Learning, Literacy and Engagement, I have the privilege of leading a team of talented colleagues who create programs and experiences that help people connect with the Library — whether they’re visiting in person, joining online or engaging from their own communities. Our work spans the offices of Library Events, Signature Programs, Informal Learning, Literary Initiatives, Visitor Engagement, and Professional Learning and Outreach Initiatives, all shaped by a deep and ongoing understanding of our audiences.

In my role, I focus on setting direction and creating the conditions for this work to thrive. That includes building consistent, audience-focused programming frameworks — like Live! At the Library, Afternoons With the Library and Family Days — that give people welcoming, predictable ways to engage. These platforms also make it easier for colleagues across the Library to bring their ideas to life and reach the audiences they care about.

title: Introducing CARaL: Copyright Anxiety, Resilience and Leadership
content:
Many of you will know that Chris and I have been working for some time on research into Copyright Anxiety and Legal Chill. Therefore we are really excited to launch a new collaboration this autumn with the author, coach and trainer, Helen Rimmer. Helen is the author of the Facet book The Kind Librarian and her work on leadership and compassion really struck a chord with our findings that were emerging from the copyright anxiety research.

What’s CARaL all about?

CARaL: Copyright Anxiety, Resilience and Leadership is a new four-part online programme exploring something that traditional copyright training rarely addresses: the emotional, cultural and leadership impact of copyright work.

Copyright is a technical subject, but it is also felt emotionally. The fear of getting something wrong can lead to anxiety, over-checking, unnecessary escalation and what we’re calling “Legal Chill” – where over-caution begins to become a barrier to access, innovation and creativity.

title: EFF and Civil Society Groups Call on Nottinghamshire Police to Halt Live Face Recognition
content:
This week, EFF, along with Big Brother Watch, Defend Digital Me, Liberty, Open Rights Group, Race Equality First, Statewatch, and Stopwatch, wrote to Nottinghamshire Police Force in the UK raising concern about the proposed roll-out of live facial recognition technology (LFR), and called for its immediate halt.

In particular, the letter highlights six concerns:

Nottinghamshire Police has stated that “facial recognition is just another tool to fight crime.” But LFR used in public spaces is an incredibly intrusive biometric mass surveillance technology that scans the faces of everyone who walks past the camera and takes biometric face prints. This is not just another tool, but a major escalation of surveillance that treats everyone as a suspect by default.

title: Information Integrity in crisis: Why South Africa’s Human Rights body is taking action
content:
By Janet Heard

The South African Human Rights Commission (SAHRC) has released a policy brief on safeguarding information integrity as a precondition for rights, including a recommendation to strengthen support for pluralistic and independent media.

By doing so, the SAHRC policy brief on Information Integrity and Human Rights mirrors calls in the Johannesburg Declaration, which was adopted during the inaugural M20 (Media) Summit in South Africa in September last year.

A rights-centred framework is a cornerstone of the M20 Declaration, which references human rights eight times. It notes that information integrity is both in crisis and essential to sustaining democracy. “Our call is an injunction to everyone to do more to protect press freedom, and support the role of journalism, and a human rights-based media ecosystem in its contribution to the public good.”

In turn, the SAHRC brief focuses on disinformation, platform accountability, and democratic resilience in South Africa. “In contexts where access to reliable, independent information is limited, disinformation is more likely to take root and spread, particularly among marginalised and linguistically underserved communities.’

title: Poll: The older and richer you are, the more you like AI
content:
LONDON — Increasing age and financial security correspond to increasing positivity towards AI and what it can bring, according new polling from Public First shared with POLITICO.

The least positive age group are 18 to 24-year-olds who are concerned about the technology’s impact on their own thinking skills and career progression. Although the heaviest users of the tech, more than a third of 18-24s worry that AI will make critical thinking harder, and exactly a third think developing career-relevant expertise will become more difficult, finds the polling.

The age group was the most pessimistic across all career-related issues, spanning independent problem solving and learning from mentors.

Compare the young adults to the 35 to 44-year olds, who use the tech as heavily as their younger counterparts, and a divergence is clear: only 19 percent of 18-24s think AI will improve both their own opportunities and society, whereas 28 percent of the older group does. The AI tools available are the same, but the older group already have career experience and expertise.

title: Hong Kong: Unjust verdict against Chow Hang-Tung uses draconian law, silences dissent
content:
CIVICUS global civil society alliance condemns the guilty verdict against Chow Hang-Tung. The human rights defender was criminalised for ‘subversion’ under the draconian national security law. We reiterate our longstanding calls for her immediate and unconditional release and demand an end to the repression against human rights activists in the territory. 

Chow Hang-Tung is a human rights lawyer and pro-democracy activist featured in CIVICUS’ Stand As My Witness Campaign. She was one of the four vice-chairs of the now-defunct Hong Kong Alliance in Support of the Patriotic Democratic Movement of China (HKA). The HKA led the organisation of the annual Tiananmen vigils marking the brutal Tiananmen Massacre in 1989.

title: Hong Kong: Activists Convicted for Tiananmen Vigils
content:
(New York) – The Hong Kong High Court convicted two activists who have long advocated for justice for the victims of China’s 1989 Tiananmen Massacre, Human Rights Watch said today. Hong Kong authorities should quash the convictions, which violate the defendants’ rights to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly.

On August 21, 2026, the court convicted Chow Hang-tung, 41, and Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, former leaders of the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China, the now-disbanded organizer of the city’s annual vigil commemorating the massacre. They were convicted of “inciting subversion” under Hong Kong’s National Security Law. A third former leader, Albert Ho, 74, had pleaded guilty to the same charge in January. They face up to 10 years in prison.

“The conviction of these Tiananmen vigil organizers shows that public displays of mourning have become a crime in Hong Kong,” said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “These activists exposed how the Chinese government fears the memory of its own atrocities and treats remembrance as a national security threat.”

title: The Alps are breaking apart and glaciers are vanishing. The consequences are already economic
content:
When protective winter snow melted off Switzerland’s Alpine glaciers on 29 June 2026, marking the second earliest Glacier Loss Day in recorded history, few people paid much attention.

Winter snow acts as a shield — it reflects sunlight and protects the ice beneath. This past winter brought little of it, so it melted early, and the sun began attacking ice that had built up over centuries.

Less than two months later, the problem is far more tangible. Rivers across central Europe are running at historic lows. The loss of the Alps’ natural water reservoir is shifting from a long-term climate risk to a concrete economic problem — disrupting river transport, energy production and industrial supply chains from Bavaria to the Black Sea.

Switzerland is the continent’s natural water tower, and the rate at which it is losing glacial mass has entered a critical phase, according to Matthias Huss, head of the Swiss glacier monitoring network GLAMOS, and researchers at ETH Zürich.

title: From denial to exploitation: how the Kremlin has adapted its climate disinformation
content:
In the latest wave of climate-related narratives spread by the Kremlin, climate change is a vehicle to reinforce familiar disinformation tropes: the alleged authoritarianism and hypocrisy of the EU, Europe’s supposed self-inflicted decline through sanctions against Russia, and, ultimately, the claim that Europe has no choice but to restore relations with Russia as a supplier of affordable oil and gas.

Climate change used to be a fringe topic in Kremlin propaganda. It was rarely mentioned, and when it was, it was often accompanied by absurd claims or outright denial. But as the effects of climate change become increasingly difficult to ignore (including domestically in Russia), pro-Kremlin outlets have largely stopped denying its existence. Instead, they have woven it into their disinformation ecosystem, shifting from denying the problem to discrediting proposed solutions.

title: Missouri Republicans Are Trying to Repeal Abortion Rights by Leaning Into Anti-Trans Sentiment
content:
Two years ago, abortion opponents in Missouri tried to defeat Amendment 3, a ballot initiative to enshrine reproductive rights in the state constitution, by falsely telling voters that it would allow gender transition surgeries for minors — even though it wouldn’t.

Voters approved Amendment 3 anyway, overturning the near-total abortion ban enacted by Missouri’s GOP-dominated legislature that had taken effect after the U.S. Supreme Court struck down Roe v. Wade in 2022.

Now Republican leaders in the state are trying to repeal those rights again, using the same issue. They placed a new amendment on the November ballot, also called Amendment 3, that would restore Missouri’s abortion ban while allowing limited exceptions but also constitutionally prohibit gender transition care for minors — though the state has banned surgeries and new prescriptions of puberty blockers and hormones by law since August 2023.

title: Women in politics face more personal, sexualised attacks than men, a recent analysis shows
content:
Online spaces, and social media in particular, are forums for vigorous political debate. They provide a space for members of the public to express political opinions, organise, and sometimes even interact directly with politicians. While they clearly have democratising potential, these platforms have also become fertile ground for hate speech, toxic interactions and online violence.

By analysing over 3.2 million responses on X (formerly Twitter) to 88 candidates for the 2024 European Parliament elections, our team at the European Commission’s Joint Research Centre have found significant differences in how women and men in politics get treated online.

Applying a toxicity detection algorithm called Perspective API, we studied both the volume and types of “toxic” replies received by different candidates. The algorithm’s toxicity score ranges from zero to one. It estimates the likelihood that a reader would perceive text as toxic, and defines toxicity as “a rude, disrespectful, or unreasonable comment that is likely to make you leave a discussion”.

title: We’re building a New York-sized city every month. That’s worrying for our climate
content:
Each of us needs of a roof over our head, classrooms to learn in and offices or space to work from.

To meet this unprecedented demand for new buildings, globally we’re constructing the equivalent of an entire New York City every month.

This provides us with vital infrastructure, but also generates an enormous amount of world-warming emissions.

So how can we build what we need, without harming our planet? Our new research provides some answers.

Creating new buildings benefits communities, cities and countries, and eases housing pressure. That’s why Australia’s National Housing Accord is aiming to construct 1.2 million new, well-located homes between 2024 and 2029.

But this Australian effort is dwarfed by the 96,000 new and affordable homes needed worldwide every single day. Tragically, hundreds of millions of people around the world endure homelessness. One in four are living in harmful conditions.

However, construction comes with a climate cost. Each time we build, we use materials and construction processes that release large amounts of greenhouse gas emissions – known as “embodied carbon”.

title: How changing diets are creating new markets for Africa’s Indigenous crops
content:
As health-conscious consumers increasingly look beyond wheat, Africa’s Indigenous crops are finding new commercial value.

Originally published on Global Voices

Packaged Cassava and Potato flour. Photo by Bonface Orucho. Used with permission.

This story was written by Bonface Orucho and originally published by Bird Story Agency on July 28, 2026. This revised version is republished below as part of a content-sharing agreement. It is also part of Global Voices’ August 2026 Spotlight series, “Indigenous Rights.” You can support this coverage by donating here.

Wheat has long dominated Africa’s bakeries. But inside Nairobi’s Kirsten Bakery, shelves increasingly feature breads, cakes, and pastries made from naturally gluten-free ingredients such as cassava, millet, and sorghum.

The bakery is one example of a broader shift unfolding across Africa, where changing consumer preferences are creating new commercial opportunities for entrepreneurs, food scientists, and manufacturers to transform Indigenous crops into premium food products.

title: Governments Should Protect Environmental Defenders from Violence and Repression
content:
As space for environmental advocacy rapidly shrinks, Indigenous peoples, climate activists, and land defenders increasingly face harassment, criminalization, and repression for protecting lands, ecosystems, and communities from environmental harm. The use of violence, intimidation, and threats to silence environmental defenders is an urgent challenge. 

Against this backdrop, the UN Special Rapporteur on the right to a healthy environment is compiling a report on environmental defenders worldwide, to which Human Rights Watch submitted input on August 19. 

In Brazil, HRW has extensively documented how criminal networks engaged in illegal deforestation, mining, and land-grabbing threaten and sometimes kill Indigenous people, small farmers, and environmental agents who stand in their way. HRW also documented police beating defenders peacefully protesting mining in Indonesia.

title: Coffee at 330%, citrus at 85%: EU study maps what happens when banned pesticide residues are blocked from imports
content:
That is the central finding of a study by researchers at the European Commission’s Joint Research Centre (JRC).

The agency turned to this question because the Commission, in its Vision for Agriculture and Food presented last year, pledged to require imported food to meet the same standards as those applicable within the EU. “The Commission will establish a principle that the most hazardous pesticides banned in the EU for health and environmental reasons are not allowed back to the EU through imported products,” the Vision states. The executive reaffirmed this commitment this year when it presented its agricultural and food simplification package.

What the ban would cause depends first on whether growers outside the EU would choose to adapt to European standards, reduce their exports to Europe, or stop them altogether.

That was also a challenge for the authors of the analysis, which is why they estimate the consequences across three different scenarios.

The most pessimistic scenario is that producers would not stop using the banned pesticides, effectively closing the gates of the European market to them.

Agricultural imports into the EU would in that case fall by as much as 41 percent.

title: Oregon Is Spending More Than Ever on Low-Income Housing. A State Law Keeps the Details Secret.
content:
Oregon’s spending on low-income housing has exploded in the past five years. The state has given developers an unprecedented $1.4 billion, and the cost of developing each apartment has nearly doubled, to $540,000. Dozens of projects are lined up for an additional $850 million in future state funding. Federal tax credits, which the state oversees, will bring even more money to bear.

Yet one thing has remained constant: The public isn’t allowed to see the details of how all these dollars are being spent.

Oregon is one of the only states in the country with a carve-out in its public records law that prevents disclosing the financial details of subsidized housing projects, thwarting researchers and journalists who have tried to examine their costs.

The issue is especially pressing in the Pacific Northwest, where leaders have tied the lack of affordable housing to the region’s dire homelessness crisis. Understanding and controlling the cost of construction could make it possible, with the same amount of money, to either build more rent-restricted apartments or to discount rents more steeply.

title: Kysely: Afrikkalaisnuoret uskovat Trumpin olevan heille hyväksi – ”Nuoret ovat väsyneitä kaunopuheeseen, joka ei johda mihinkään”
content:
Jopa 60 prosenttia afrikkalaisnuorista suhtautuu optimistisesti Yhdysvaltojen presidentin Donald Trumpin toiseen kauteen.

Nuorisobarometri African Youth Survey 2026 haastatteli noin 5 000:ta afrikkalaisnuorta 16 maassa. Etenkin nuorison voimaantuminen, sotilaallinen tuki, turvallisuusyhteistyö ja terrorismin vastainen työ nähtiin alueina, joilla Trumpilla voisi olla positiivinen vaikutus.  

Tulokset voi nähdä yllätyksellisinä siinä valossa, että samassa tutkimuksessa pari vuotta sitten vastaajat näkivät Joe Bidenin presidenttiyden parempana asiana Afrikalle kuin Trumpin. Trump on sen lisäksi useasti puhunut halventavasti Afrikan maista, ajanut alas USAID-järjestön, eli yhdysvaltalaisen avustusjärjestelmän, ja julkisesti himonnut mantereen mineraaleja.   

Nämä asiat myös huolestuttivat vastaajien keskuudessa. Noin kolme viidestä pelkäsi Yhdysvaltojen sivuuttavan kansainvälisiä lait ja normit päästääkseen käsiksi luonnonresursseihin. Tämä huoli oli vielä suurempi Etelä-Afrikassa ja Liberiassa.

Vajaa puolet vastaajista myös näki USAID-alasajon huonona asiana maalleen, mutta toisaalta moni toivoi sen tuovan positiivista muutosta maiden omiin kykyihin ottaa ohjat terveydenhuollossa.

title: Chad: Political Opponents Freed
content:
(New York) – The Chadian authorities should vacate or set aside the conviction of Succès Masra, the former Chadian prime minister and main opposition leader, Human Rights Watch said today. Masra was released from prison on August 15, 2026, after receiving a presidential pardon.

His pardon and those of eight other political opponents led to their release from prison. However, their convictions for conduct that was legitimate political expression still stand and need to be set aside so they can continue to participate in politics. 

“The release of Masra and other political opponents is good news,” said Lewis Mudge, Central Africa director at Human Rights Watch. “But to be clear, Masra was arrested on trumped-up charges in an attempt to silence him. The Chadian authorities should go beyond the presidential pardon and ensure that his conviction is set aside.”

title: Spain: Humanitarian and Rights Crisis in Ceuta
content:
(Milan) – The Spanish government and local authorities in its North African enclave Ceuta should act urgently to provide adequate shelter to all migrants and asylum seekers living unsheltered since entering Ceuta from Morocco at the end of July, Human Rights Watch said today. The authorities should provide the opportunity to apply for asylum for those who want to.

“Thousands of people have been in the streets in a legal vacuum, exposed to sexual violence and without adequate shelter, food, or sanitation for almost three weeks,” said Judith Sunderland, senior associate director for refugee and migrant rights at Human Rights Watch. “Despite the challenging situation, Spain should quickly mobilize sufficient resources to ensure humane and orderly management of the crisis for the good of migrants and Ceuta residents alike.”

During a four-day research trip to Ceuta, from August 15 to 18, Human Rights Watch spoke with 76 migrants, including 42 individual interviews (37 adults and 5 unaccompanied children) and group or brief conversations with 34, including 4 unaccompanied children.

title: Who’s Afraid of Chinese Surpluses?
content: China recorded the largest trade surplus in history last year, and its exports continue to grow. But the scale of the threat to the global economy, and the appropriate response, remains subject to considerable disagreement. Some economists advocate protectionist measures, if only to pressure China to commit to economic rebalancing, others argue that tariffs won’t help, and still others think the specter of another “China shock” is a bogeyman, because China’s surpluses do more good than harm.

title: 10 ungewöhnliche Orte, an denen Menschen zur Wikipedia beitragen
content: Im polnischen Zabrze fand 2025 ein Edit-a-thon im Guido-Bergwerk statt – 320 Meter unter Tage. In den Räumen einer ehemaligen Kohlemine schrieben und verbesserten 84 Wikipedianer*innen gemeinsam Artikel über das Erbe Schlesiens. Und das gleich in vier Sprachen: Polnisch, Schlesisch, Tschechisch und Deutsch. Das Guido-Bergwerk sei ein Juwel des industriellen Erbes der Region, heißt es von den Organisator*innen von Wikimedia Polska. Ziel des Edit-a-thons war, das Wissen über das Erbe der Woiwodschaft Schlesien in Wikipedia zu erweitern: „Wikipedianerinnen und Wikipedianer dokumentieren das, was sonst oft übersehen wird – lokale Persönlichkeiten, alte Traditionen, verschwindende Ortsnamen. Dank ihnen wird das Wissen über die Region Teil des globalen Informationsflusses.“

title: Relax, everyone: Elon Musk has a mantra to make the climate crisis go away | Emma Brockes
content:
It’s simple, says the SpaceX boss – according to something called the ‘Kardashev scale’, we just have to move energy production ‘off-planet’

Next time the weather gives the UK 61 days without rain and we wonder idly if this is the end, there is a term we may whistle up to soothe us. Like murmuring the rosary, or putting our fingers in our ears and humming, this phrase is to be mumbled on repeat – “the Kardashev scale, the Kardashev scale” – a buzzy concept in tech, much favoured by Elon Musk, and precisely the thing we’ve been waiting for. The Kardashev scale is the answer both to our impending doom and our anxiety around it – and if we decide to believe in it, we won’t have to give the climate crisis a single thought until the last drip falls from the tap.

title: From conference grant to career milestone: the journey to an Early Career Research Award
content:
In July 2026, Vancouver, Canada hosted the 10th World Congress of Biomechanics (WCB26), the world’s leading congress on biomechanics and mechanobiology, organised every four years. This edition has been jointly organised by the European Society of Biomechanics, the American Society of Biomechanics and the Canadian Society of Biomechanics. WCB provides the latest research outputs on biomechanics and brings together researchers and scientists expert in wearable sensors, artificial intelligence, regenerative medicine, and novel devices, to name a few.

ESB awards promote excellence in biomechanics research to foster integration of clinical and basic science, and to facilitate the translation of that science to health care and clinical practice.

The ESB Early Career Research Award, initiated in 2023, recognises the development of an outstanding young researcher in the process of career consolidation, who contributes to the advancement of the theory and/or applications of Biomechanics and/or mechanobiology.

title: Ny öppen webbkurs utmanar missuppfattningar om islam
content:
I traditionella och sociala medier sprids många missuppfattningar om begrepp och företeelser som förknippas med islam, vilket försvårar en konstruktiv diskussion. Kursen betonar mångfalden inom islam och bland muslimer”, berättar universitetslektor och docent Ilkka Lindstedt vid Helsingfors universitet, som var med och förverkligade kursen. ‘A data engineering approach to tracking global climate resilience’ outlines the challenges related to developing consistent, efficient, and accurate methods for assessing the Belém indicators (adopted at the 30th United Nations Climate Change Conference in November 2025) for measuring progress towards climate resilience.  Also described are how the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF), the CDIF4EOSC project and other tools and methods supported by CODATA can help realise meet these challenges.

 
The article was written by Bapon Fakhruddin, co-chair of the CODATA FAIR Data for Disaster Risk Research Task Group, with input from Matti Heikkurinen, CODATA Project Portfolio Manager.

content:
Frame ja Suomen Kulttuurirahasto järjestävät marraskuussa 2026 opintomatkan 16. Dak’Art – Dakarin biennaaliin Senegaliin ja Marrakechiin, Marokkoon. Osallistujat matkalle valittiin nykytaiteen ammattilaisille suunnatulla avoimella haulla.

Opintomatkalle valittiin Seinäjoen taidehallin taidetuottaja Pii Anttila, HIAP – Helsinki International Artist Programmen johtaja Emma Beverley, itsenäinen kuraattori Chih-Tung Lin, EMMA – Espoon modernin taiteen museon intendentti Ingrid Orman ja Aboa Vetus Ars Novan näyttelypäällikkö Terhi Tuomi. Ulkomaille suuntautuvien opintomatkojen tarkoituksena on muodostaa kuva kohdemaiden taidekentästä, vierailla kansainvälisissä nykytaidetapahtumissa, rakentaa verkostoja sekä kartoittaa mahdollisia yhteistyökumppaneita.

title: Kolumni: Kirjastoissa otettiin lukuaskeleita
content:
Viimeisen vuoden aikana olemme matkustaneet ympäri Suomea, istuneet tunteja niin junissa, busseissa kuin ajoittain takseissa. Olemme nähneet kaupunkeja auringonlaskun jälkeen ja ihailleet vanhoja, upeita hotelleja hiljentyneillä paikkakunnilla. Ensimmäisen hankematkan alkaessa emme tienneet mitä odottaa. Satojen kilometrien jälkeen voimme todeta, että lukuaskeleiden ottaminen oli rankkaa, mutta palkitsevaa.

Kirjastoseuran tekemän lukutaitotyösuosituksen mukaan lukutaitotyö tarkoittaa lukutaidon ylläpitoa, syventämistä ja harjaannuttamista. Tätä suositusta ja kansallista lukutaitostrategiaa lähdimme jalkauttamaan yleisiin kirjastoihin Kirjaston lukuaskel -nimisen hankkeen kautta.

Tavoitteena oli kehittää kirjastoille helposti toteutettava työpajamalli, jonka avulla ne voivat laatia oman lukutaitotyösuunnitelmansa sekä tehdä työtään näkyväksi kunnan asiakirjoissa.

Viime syksystä alkaen työpajoja on toteutettu eri puolilla Suomea. Niiden avulla kirkastettiin kirjastojen tekemää lukutaitotyötä sekä henkilökunnalle että asiakkaille. Työpajassa ei luoda uusia toimintatapoja, vaan tunnistetaan ja jäsennetään jo olemassa olevia käytäntöjä ja yhteistyön muotoja.

title: Kulttuurikunnilla on lumovoimaa
content:
Minulla oli tänä kesänä ilo osallistua neljäntoista pienen ja keskisuuren kulttuurikunnan Elinvoimaa kulttuurista -verkoston kokoukseen Pietarsaaressa. Joukossa on useita kaupunkeja, joilla on vahva kulttuuribrändi.

Verkoston aloitteentekijöitä ovat muun muassa kokeneet yliopistolaiset Seija Kulkki ja Yrjö Sotamaa. Verkosto onkin julkaissut useita pamfletteja, jotka antavat kunnille välineitä luoda kulttuurista elinvoimaa. Pamfletit löytyvät Yrjö Sotamaan sivuilta.

Itsetyytyväiseen lekotteluun ei ole varaa missään, sillä kaikkialla Suomessa kulttuuri- ja taide-elämä tarvitsee myös julkista rahoitusta. Kunnat ja valtio rahoittavat kulttuuria ja taidetta jokseenkin yhtä paljon. Kuntien taloustilanteet tietysti vaihtelevat, mutta harvassa paikassa on rahaa ongelmaksi asti. Valtiontalouden tilanne on valitettavan hyvin tiedossa.

Verkoston tapaamisessa kuultiin useita eteenpäinkatsovia puheenvuoroja siitä, miten kulttuuri voi toimia ratkaisuna, jonka avulla kunnan elinvoimaa – vetovoimaa, pitovoimaa ja lumovoimaa – lisätään, mutta se vaatii myös kulttuuritoimijoilta uusiutumis- ja yhteistyökykyä.

title: Paikalliset helmet ja tarinat esillä Kulttuuriympäristöpäivien tapahtumissa
content:
Kulttuuriympäristöpäivät kutsuvat tutustumaan kiinnostaviin rakennuksiin, maisemiin, tapoihin ja tarinoihin eri puolilla Suomea. Elokuun lopulta marraskuulle järjestettävien tapahtumien joukossa on paljon maksutonta ohjelmaa. Katso mitä omalla lähiseudullasi tapahtuu!

Syksyn aikana ympäri Suomea avautuu ovia kiinnostaviin rakennuksiin ja paikkakuntien tarinoihin, kun Kulttuuriympäristöpäiviä vietetään elokuun lopulta marraskuulle.

Tapahtumissa pääsee tutustumaan alueen rakennusperintöön opastetuilla kierroksilla, avoimien ovien päivissä, näyttelyissä, kävelyretkillä ja muissa yleisötapahtumissa. Samalla tapahtumat muistuttavat siitä, miten rakennettu ympäristö vaikuttaa paikalliseen identiteettiin, viihtyvyyteen ja yhteisöllisyyteen.

Kulttuuriympäristöpäivät on Euroopan laajin yleisötapahtumien kokonaisuus, jonka tarkoituksena on tehdä rakennuksia, maisemia, tapoja ja tarinoita tutuksi kaikille. Valtaosa päivien tapahtumista on maksuttomia.

title: Muistoseminaari Markku Tannerin elämäntyön kunniaksi
content:
Viime syksynä kuolleen Suomen Kotiseutuliiton pitkäaikaisen toiminnanjohtajan, järjestöneuvos Markku Tannerin (1943–2025) elämäntyön kunniaksi järjestetään muistoseminaari torstaina 8. lokakuuta klo 13–16.

Tilaisuus on kaikille avoin ja maksuton ja se pidetään Helsingissä Karjalatalossa, os. Käpylänkuja 1. Tilaisuuteen voi osallistua vain paikan päällä eikä sitä striimata verkkoon.

Tannerin kuoleman vuosipäivänä pidettävän seminaarin alustukset kytkeytyvät kolmeen hänelle tärkeään teemaan: karjalaisuuteen, kaupunkilaisuuteen ja yhteisöllisyyteen. Paneelikeskustelussa rakennetaan tulevaisuuspolkuja Tannerin viitoittamalla tiellä.

Seminaarin puheenjohtajana toimii Kotiseutuliiton puheenjohtaja, professori emerita Laura Kolbe. Omaisten puheenvuoron käyttää toimittaja Matti Tanner.

Muistoseminaarin järjestävät yhteistyössä yhdeksän järjestöä: Suomen Kotiseutuliitto, Karjalan Liitto, Karjalaisen Kulttuurin Edistämissäätiö, Karjalainen Nuorisoliitto, Lauttasaari-Seura, Kalevalaseura, Karjalainen Osakunta, Wiipurilainen Osakunta sekä Seniores Carelienses.

title: Algorithms in Reflection
content:
Algorithms in Reflection ist ein interaktiver Spiegel, der auf Gesichtsausdrücke reagiert. Besucher*innen sehen ihr Spiegelbild nur, wenn das System ein Lächeln erkennt: Ein Rollo öffnet sich und gibt den Spiegel frei – sobald das Lächeln verschwindet, verschwindet auch das Spiegelbild.

Die Arbeit schafft eine einfache, zugleich ungewohnte Begegnung: Nicht ein Mensch reagiert auf einen Gesichtsausdruck, sondern eine Maschine entscheidet, ob dieser überzeugend genug ist. So wird erfahrbar, wie es sich anfühlt, von einem System erkannt und durch Daten interpretiert zu werden.

Die Installation lenkt den Blick auf Technologien, die zunehmend Gesichter, Gesten und Verhalten analysieren und hinterfragt zugleich die Bedeutung emotionalen Ausdrucks. Ein Lächeln kann Freude, Höflichkeit, Beruhigung oder soziale Erwartungen vermitteln – spontan entstehen oder bewusst inszeniert sein.

Im Umgang mit dem Spiegel wird sichtbar, wie Maschinen Menschen interpretieren und wie Menschen lernen, sich selbst zu präsentieren. Was geschieht, wenn sich unsere Ausdrucksformen nicht mehr an andere Menschen richten, sondern an Algorithmen?

title: Discover the Mundaneum, an Early 20th-Century “Internet” That Put the World’s Knowledge on Millions of Index Cards
content: Pitch to friends or family the idea of a trip to Mons, Belgium to visit the Mundaneum, and you may be met with a less-than-enthusiastic reception. That’s unfortunate, since such an experience could fundamentally change the way they regard technology they use every day. Though its name may seem to promise unrelieved dullness today, the Mundaneum arose out of enormous high-tech ambitions. The idea behind it, as conceived by Belgian lawyers Paul Otlet and Henri La Fontaine, was to gather, classify, centralize, and make universally available all human knowledge. This may sound familiar to anyone who’s used the internet, but it was a rather bolder proposition at the turn of the twentieth century.

title: It’s Never Too Early to Think About Your Legacy
content:
The Internet Archive has cultivated thousands of planned giving supporters over the years who have decided when making their legacy plans to include the Internet Archive in them as a nonprofit of choice. Tim, who turned 40, made that decision and decided it was time to think about the organizations that reflect what matters most to him and how he could help sustain their work.

He named the Internet Archive as one of his primary beneficiaries, making him a member of the Internet Archive Legacy Circle.

Tim grew up alongside the early internet. He built homepages, joined web rings, learned HTML, and eventually turned that early curiosity into a career working with Linux and open-source technology. “The internet, for me, is like a forest that I’ve grown up in, and I’ve seen change over time.”

Today, the Wayback Machine allows Tim to revisit some of the websites, blogs, and projects he created when he was younger. He also helps preserve the web by running Archive Warrior projects on his own server and regularly uses the Live Music Archive.

Tim, Internet Archive Legacy Circle Member and Monthly Giving Circle Member

title: The Supreme Court’s 1954 Brown v. Board Ruling: “A Day That Will Live in Glory”
content:
-This article also appears in the May/June issue of the Library of Congress Magazine, which focused on momentous events in the nation’s first 250 years.

The Supreme Court’s ruling in Brown v. Board of Education on May 17, 1954, was one of the most consequential decisions in American history and is exhaustively documented at the Library. A unanimous court emphatically ruled that the “separate but equal” doctrine of the 1896 Plessy v. Ferguson Supreme Court ruling — the basis for legalized segregation in the United States — was a false premise and always had been.

“We conclude that in the field of public education ‘separate but equal’ has no place,” Chief Justice Earl Warren wrote in his opinion, underlining the last phrase in his reading copy. Then he delivered the hammer blow, underlining the entire next sentence: “Separate educational facilities are inherently unequal.”

The case, though focused on public schools, would apply to every facet of American life. No more “Colored Only” water fountains. The nation was entering a new era.

title: Workshop on Policies for the Knowledge Commons
content:
On 22 July, Open Future partnered with Inria to host a workshop at Inria’s Paris offices, exploring a shared EU policy agenda for the knowledge commons. The workshop took place against the backdrop of the European Commission’s consultation around an Open Digital Ecosystem Strategy and the subsequent Tech Sovereignty Package. These initiatives have shaped recent discussions on digital sovereignty.

The session brought together representatives from commons projects, such as Wikipedia and Software Heritage; research institutions including CNRS; organizations such as OpenMined, along with policymakers and allied stakeholders.The workshop addressed a gap in the current EU digital sovereignty debate. While policy attention has focused heavily on open-source software, knowledge commons projects, such as Wikipedia and OpenStreetMap, which are foundational layers of the knowledge infrastructure relied on by both human understanding and AI systems, remain underrepresented. These projects face unique challenges regarding sustainability, licensing, and reciprocity that existing policy frameworks do not adequately address.

title: Slow Regulation on AI-Generated CSAM is Failing its Victims
content:
“I just love knowing that the quality… as great as it is at this point, it’s only going to get better!” A random user shares his excitement about a new generative AI tool, without mentioning the gruesome and disturbing purpose for which it is intended. Across both openly accessible forums and the dark web, child sex offenders are increasingly celebrating recent advances in artificial intelligence used to generate child sexual abuse material (CSAM).

“Generating on-topic [CSAM] content is the same as any other content, just with a different prompt. After that it’s just a lot of experimentation!”, another user writes, according to conversations collected by the Internet Watch Foundation (IWF), a UK organization advocating for eliminating online CSAM and protecting victims. “Offenders see themselves as part of a community that helps one another. Everything is said with such enthusiasm, and there is absolutely no sense of shame,” says Catherine McShane, the IWF’s press officer.

title: Intermediary Liability in Brazil: The Intricate Path Ahead
content:
Brazil's new internet intermediary liability regime is underway. The implementation of changes established by the Supreme Court includes notice and takedown mechanisms and duty of care obligations. Caution is crucial as these measures can create problematic incentives for enforcement overreach and over censorship of protected speech.  

The court in June issued a new decision clarifying elements of its 2025 finding that the previous liability regime was partially unconstitutional. The government also published in late May two presidential decrees that detail how the new rules apply. 

Under the new regime, social media platforms and other internet applications that curate or interfere with posts can be held liable for third-party content if they don’t remove it after being notified by the user seeking take down unless there's a reasonable doubt that the content is unlawful. For certain specific cases, like crimes against honor (e.g. defamation), platform liability still depends on failing to comply with a judicial order.

title: LAYING THE GROUNDWORK FOR AI-POWERED CYBERSECURITY

Easier to build, faster to launch and more destructive than ever before, cyberattacks are getting a significant boost from frontier artificial intelligence (AI) models.

That was the message from European Union (EU) digital chief Henna Virkkunen at the early July 2026 launch of the EU’s Action Plan on Cybersecurity and Artificial Intelligence.

Virkkunen raised concerns that advanced AI models can now build cyber exploits in minutes or hours, posing a direct threat to the security of critical infrastructure and society at large.

While AI is a powerful asset for attackers, it is also a powerful tool for defenders.

This post is part of Global Voices’ August 2026 Spotlight series, “Indigenous Rights.” This series offers insight into the lives and experiences of Indigenous peoples to build connections across regions, center Indigenous experiences, and share the stories of leaders, activists, community members, and more. You can support this coverage by donating here.

The majority of the world’s languages are primarily spoken, not written. So, the knowledge of the speaker communities is oral, yet Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects require written citations.

The OpenSpeaks Archives is developing a process for Wikimedians to cite oral knowledge from Indigenous and other low-resourced language communities, including nearly 20 language communities from India, Nepal, and Sri Lanka. This process includes audio-visual documentation, creating technological and educational resources, and community capacity building.

title: Jailed Journalist in Azerbaijan Denied Medical Care
content:
Azerbaijani authorities are refusing to allow a jailed journalist with a serious breathing disorder to see a specialist or to undergo diagnostic scans, her family and lawyer say, the latest sign of the deteriorating conditions for the country’s imprisoned journalists.

Aytac Ahmadova, 32, who writes as Aytac Tapdig, is a reporter for the exiled outlet Meydan TV. She has been in pretrial detention at Kurdakhani Prison since December 6, 2024, when she was arrested with five Meydan TV colleagues in raids, days after Azerbaijan hosted the COP29 climate summit. She was initially charged with currency smuggling, and later other financial crimes. 

Her ongoing trial, alongside 11 other journalists and media workers, began in December 2025 and has no verdict date.

Tapdig has a nasal condition and chronic breathing difficulties. A July 2026 letter from detention revealed that she had used 80 bottles of nasal spray and become dependent on them. The Penitentiary Service does not employ an ear, nose, and throat (ENT) specialist, she said.
